1200.author: yuanzhou75
1200.body:
Closes #1152

Stage 2 of the issue: the pipeline no longer materialises an archive on either side, the default cap moves to 5 GiB, and both sides check the machine before starting rather than failing halfway.

## What changed

**Export.** `writeResearchPackage` writes tar → gzip → the task's own file; the background export hands it a destination, so there is no whole-archive buffer, and a cancelled or failed task deletes a partial file instead of discarding one. Objects are handed over as sources — a CAS stream, or a workspace file read twice — so the payload is not all resident.

**Import.** `importResearchPackageStreamed` takes the compressed bytes as they arrive, gunzips incrementally, parses the tar sequentially and writes each object to `objectDirectory/<sha256>` while hashing it, so a digest is verified against its address before the object can be used. Manifest, records and readme are the only resident entries; the object map is backed by that directory and reads one object at a time.

**HTTP.** `POST .../research-package/inspect` and `.../import` stream the upload to `<data dir>/research-package-uploads/<purpose>-XXXX/package.sdresearch` and parse it from there. The inspection cache now owns that directory instead of a `Buffer`; a cached import deletes it only after the restore has copied the archive into its snapshot, and a read-only restore uses `copyFile(..., COPYFILE_EXCL)` instead of rewriting bytes.

**Preflight.** Each side is charged only what it writes: an export against the preview's `archiveBytes` (one compressed file, the uncompressed estimate being an upper bound); an upload against `content-length` (the staged file); a streamed parse against `min(ceiling, free disk / 3)`, which reserves the two copies a later restore adds; a restore against `2 × unpacked + records` on disk (snapshot objects and CAS blobs — the unpacked upload is already there) and `max(largest object, records) + 256 MiB` in memory. `inspect` charges nothing after its parse, because it writes nothing more. Memory is measured on `MemAvailable` so reclaimable page cache counts. Insufficient capacity is refused with HTTP 507 and `RESEARCH_PACKAGE_INSUFFICIENT_DISK` / `RESEARCH_PACKAGE_INSUFFICIENT_MEMORY`, naming what is missing.

**Cap.** Default 5 GiB, ceiling `8 GiB - 1` — the largest value an 11-digit octal tar header field can express, so the existing header writer stays valid; a single entry beyond it is refused instead of producing a broken header. The upload bound stays derived from the ceiling, as #1173 left it.

## Measurements

Incompressible payload, one object, this host (Windows, 15.7 GiB RAM), `--max-old-space-size=3072`, one process per mode, `process.resourceUsage().maxRSS` after each step:

| payload | archive | export peak — before (whole archive) | export peak — streaming | import peak — before | import peak — streaming |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| 256 MiB | 256.1 MiB | 1082 MiB | 141 MiB | 1164 MiB | 152 MiB |
| 300 MiB | 300.1 MiB | 1260 MiB | 139 MiB | 1300 MiB | 145 MiB |
| 500 MiB | 500.2 MiB | 2066 MiB | 139 MiB | 2101 MiB | 179 MiB |
| 5100 MiB (5 GiB class) | 5101.6 MiB | not run — needs ~15 GiB resident | 155 MiB | not run | 459 MiB |

The "before" column reproduces the numbers the issue measured (1071 / 1248 / 2056 MiB at 256 / 300 / 500 MiB). Times on the same runs, 256 / 300 / 500 MiB: export 11 / 15.6 / 29.4 s before and 10.6 / 15.2 / 28.5 s streaming; import 0.9 / 1.1 / 3.0 s before and 1.9 / 4.9 / 6.2 s streaming — the streamed import writes each object to disk and copies it. The 5 GiB-class round trip exported in 269 s and imported in 81 s at 155 MiB / 459 MiB peak, on a host whose `--max-old-space-size` is the API default.

## Tests

- `packages/research-package/src/index.test.ts` 16/16 and `stream-import.test.ts` 4/4: the streamed import matches the in-memory import on records, inventory and package checksum; a flipped payload byte fails the per-object digest check; a truncated archive and an over-cap archive are refused.
- `services/api/src/research-package-http.test.ts` 23/23, `research-package-exports.test.ts` 9/9 (including a failed streamed write leaving no partial archive), `conversation-branches.test.ts` 6/6, `research-package-overcap-roundtrip.test.ts` 1/1, `research-package-preflight.test.ts` 5/5.
- The tagged suites were run on this host with the `os:linux` tag relaxed for the run and restored before pushing; the tags in this commit are unchanged.
- Mutations: dropping the per-object digest check fails the tampered-payload case; removing the preflight refusal fails both refusal cases; removing the partial-file cleanup fails the write-failure case.
- `tsc -p services/api`, `tsc -p tsconfig.tests.json` and the package build are clean.

## Limits worth knowing

- A workspace file is read three times: once to name the object, once by the writer's hash pass, once by the tar pass. A CAS object is read twice. Turning the hash pass off would need the caller's checksum to be trusted; this PR does not trust it.
- The streamed import is slower per byte than the buffered one (see the times above) because each object is written to disk and then copied; that is the trade for bounded memory.
- Old packages are unaffected: the format is unchanged and an import still accepts the hard ceiling.
- No user-visible copy changed in this PR: the stage-1 limit line and over-cap confirmation are #1173, already merged. The two preflight refusals surface through the existing task error, with their message naming the missing capacity.
- The measurements above are of the package library round trip. The API restore reads one object at a time rather than materialising the package; its footprint is the largest single object plus records, which the post-parse preflight enforces.

A refusal caused by the measured free-disk budget answers HTTP 507 with `RESEARCH_PACKAGE_INSUFFICIENT_DISK` and the disk copy; an overrun of the absolute ceiling stays its own client-input error.
1200.head: fix-1152-streaming-package
1200.title: feat(research-package): stream both sides of a package and raise the cap to 5 GiB

1206.author: yuanzhou75
1206.body:
Closes #1204

## What changes

**The composer shows the permission mode and lets it be changed there.** The mode existed only behind the composer's settings menu, so what the next turn would run under was invisible until that menu was opened; the composer footer now carries a compact selector after the + and settings buttons:

- closed, it is the shield plus the mode's own word — `请求批准` with a check mark, `完全访问` with an exclamation mark and in the warning colour the flyout row already uses;
- with no session open it names what a conversation created now would run under: the project's `defaultApprovalMode`, else the global one, else `请求批准`. A default of full access is therefore shown as 完全访问 rather than 请求批准, and there is no third "follow settings" state (#1204 owner decision; the neutral label from the previous head was replaced by reading the effective default, the reviews' other allowed fix);
- open, it is the same two-row scope flyout the settings menu shows, so the scope descriptions live in one place rather than being copied;
- below 640 px it keeps the shield and drops the word: the footer is 270 px at 390 px, and a labelled third control pushed the send button outside it (the desktop-configuration journey measures exactly that), so the narrow composer uses the icon-only form the flyout still explains;
- it is disabled while a run is active, for the same reason the settings row is;
- the settings row keeps its choice: this adds a visible door, it does not remove the existing one.

**A new conversation starts in the last mode the reader selected, and that survives a restart.** `apps/desktop/src/app/approval-mode-preference.ts` keeps the choice in desktop storage under a namespaced key (`sciencediscovery-desktop:approval-mode`), next to the panel-width and locale preferences. It is read on creation, and a stored value that is not one of the two modes is treated as no choice at all. Consequences:

- conversations that already exist are never updated by it — nothing here writes to them, and reopening one only displays its own mode;
- the choice travels only in creation-time values: `CreateSessionRequest.approvalMode` for the normal path, and one best-effort `updateSession(approvalMode)` for the two paths whose conversation the service creates on its own — a new project's first conversation and an untouched draft reused by 新增会话. A failed inheritance write there never hides the conversation;
- with nothing stored, the request carries no `approvalMode` and the service default applies exactly as before.

No API change was needed: `CreateSessionRequest` already accepts `approvalMode` and the server route honours it. Permission enforcement is untouched.

## Tests

- `apps/desktop/tests/approval-mode-preference.test.ts`: 3 cases — a fresh call after `rememberApprovalMode` carries the mode (this is what a restart looks like, because the module keeps no state of its own); a stored value that is not a mode is ignored; `inheritForSession` applies the remembered mode to a conversation created by another path and makes no request when nothing is remembered.
- `apps/desktop/tests/composer.test.tsx`: 30 cases, three covering this change — the selector's position after the + and settings buttons with the asking label and check, the full-access warning colour and label, and the popover's two scope explanations with the callback receiving `ask_for_dangerous` when that row is chosen.
- `tsc -p apps/desktop/tsconfig.json --noEmit` and the root `tsc -p tsconfig.tests.json --noEmit`: clean. `pnpm ci:l1` and the rest of the gate are CI's evidence.

## Verification of the restart requirement

This was the one acceptance criterion the first head missed, so it is stated explicitly: the choice is written to `localStorage` on every selection (`sciencediscovery-desktop:approval-mode`), and the capture run below read it back after selecting full access (`stored: "always_allow"`). A fresh module instance reads it through `readStoredText`, which is what a new application process does; the unit test uses a storage stub to exercise exactly that read.

## Screenshots

| state | en | zh |
| --- | --- | --- |
| before (composer, no selector) | ![before, en](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/yuanzhou75/sciencediscovery/screenshots-1204/docs/screenshots/1204/1204-en-before.png) | ![before, zh](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/yuanzhou75/sciencediscovery/screenshots-1204/docs/screenshots/1204/1204-zh-before.png) |
| closed, 请求批准 (shield + check) | ![ask, en](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/yuanzhou75/sciencediscovery/screenshots-1204/docs/screenshots/1204/1204-en-ask.png) | ![ask, zh](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/yuanzhou75/sciencediscovery/screenshots-1204/docs/screenshots/1204/1204-zh-ask.png) |
| closed, 完全访问 (warning colour) | ![full, en](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/yuanzhou75/sciencediscovery/screenshots-1204/docs/screenshots/1204/1204-en-full.png) | ![full, zh](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/yuanzhou75/sciencediscovery/screenshots-1204/docs/screenshots/1204/1204-zh-full.png) |
| open flyout, both scope explanations | ![flyout, en](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/yuanzhou75/sciencediscovery/screenshots-1204/docs/screenshots/1204/1204-en-flyout.png) | ![flyout, zh](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/yuanzhou75/sciencediscovery/screenshots-1204/docs/screenshots/1204/1204-zh-flyout.png) |
| narrow (390 px), icon-only | ![narrow, en](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/yuanzhou75/sciencediscovery/screenshots-1204/docs/screenshots/1204/1204-en-narrow.png) | — |

Captured from the running desktop shell (vite dev + the repository's `e2e/fixtures` control plane), zh and en, 1440×900, on this head. The text was checked programmatically, not by eye: the DOM read back `请求批准` / `完全访问` and both scope explanations exactly, so the Chinese in these captures is the dictionary's own string rather than a re-encoded one — the #1148 failure was a transcoding bug and there is none here. The capture script also asserted the classes (`is-danger` only for full access) and that selecting full access stored `always_allow`.

1207.author: yuanzhou75
1207.body:
Closes #1205

A conversation created after the user has picked a model now starts from that model, **including after a restart**. Only an explicit pick writes the memory; opening an existing conversation reads its own model and never becomes the default for the next one.

## What changed

- **`state/storage.ts`**: `sciencediscovery-desktop:last-model`, next to the locale and panel-width preferences. Read at boot, written on every explicit pick, cleared when the catalog loses the model or empties.
- **`session-model-memory.ts`**: `modelForNewConversation` (the catalog check) plus `readRememberedModel` / `writeRememberedModel` over a `ReadableStorage`, so a missing or throwing storage degrades to instance-only memory instead of failing.
- **`use-workspace.ts`**:
  - the ref starts from storage, so a fresh process begins with the remembered model;
  - `selectModel` writes the pick *before* the session update, so a conversation created while that write is in flight already starts from it;
  - `createOpenSession` sends `settingsOverrides: { modelId }` instead of the top-level `modelId` shortcut: the shortcut also pins the session's `reviewModelId` (`services/api/src/http/index.ts:3138-3144`), while `createProjectAndOpen`'s `PATCH { modelId }` changes only the task model — both paths now change the task model only and agree;
  - a fresh draft shows the remembered model (then the project default, the global default, the first catalog model); `openSession` never writes the memory.

## Behaviour against the acceptance criteria

| Criterion | How it holds |
| --- | --- |
| A new conversation defaults to the last explicitly selected model, including after a restart | the pick is stored on selection and read at boot; the captures below reload the window and the next draft already shows it |
| A later selection is used by subsequently created conversations | every explicit pick overwrites the stored value |
| Conversations with messages keep their own model; reopening does not change the memory | `openSession` only clears the one-shot draft override and displays that conversation's `modelId` |
| An unavailable remembered model does not leave a dangling selection | `modelForNewConversation` rejects an id the catalog lost, the refresh clears the stored value, and the project/global default applies |
| Relevant automated tests | see below |

## Review round 1 (head `e62925a1`)

- **Restart persistence** (zhaozhaozz and HongyeZhou, required): implemented in storage, as above — not handed to #1204 any more.
- **Review-model split** (zhaozhaozz, required): the creation path now sends `settingsOverrides.modelId`; the project path's `PATCH { modelId }` was already task-model-only. Both paths now leave `reviewModelId` alone.
- **Wiring only tested at helper level** (zhaozhaozz, required): `workspace-model-setup.test.ts` now mounts the hook against a fake client that records bodies, and asserts the create body is `{ settingsOverrides: { modelId: "second" } }` and the project path PATCHes `{ modelId: "second" }`.
- **Indentation at `use-workspace.ts:817`** (HongyeZhou, optional): fixed.

## Screenshots

Desktop shell (vite dev + the repository's `e2e/fixtures` control plane), 1440×900, zh-CN and en. **Before**: a fresh window with the project default (Alpha). **After**: pick Beta in the composer's model menu, then **reload the window** — the next draft already shows Beta, read back from `sciencediscovery-desktop:last-model = model-beta`.

| state | en | zh |
| --- | --- | --- |
| before — project default | ![before, en](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/yuanzhou75/sciencediscovery/screenshots-1205/docs/screenshots/1205/1205-en-before.png) | ![before, zh](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/yuanzhou75/sciencediscovery/screenshots-1205/docs/screenshots/1205/1205-zh-CN-before.png) |
| after — remembered model, after a reload | ![after, en](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/yuanzhou75/sciencediscovery/screenshots-1205/docs/screenshots/1205/1205-en-after.png) | ![after, zh](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/yuanzhou75/sciencediscovery/screenshots-1205/docs/screenshots/1205/1205-zh-CN-after.png) |

The capture script read the values back from the DOM: `before="Alpha model"`, after the reload `"Beta model"`, and `localStorage["sciencediscovery-desktop:last-model"]="model-beta"` in both locales — so the Chinese captures show the dictionary's own strings, not a re-encode.

## Tests

- `apps/desktop/tests/session-model-memory.test.ts` **5/5**: the three decision cases, plus a stored pick surviving a fresh read and a missing/broken storage degrading safely.
- `apps/desktop/tests/workspace-model-setup.test.ts` **5/5**: the three existing cases, plus the create body and the project-path PATCH.
- Mutation: sending the top-level `modelId` on creation again makes the create-body case fail with the review-model reason.
- `tsc -p apps/desktop/tsconfig.json --noEmit` and `tsc -p tsconfig.tests.json --noEmit` are clean. The tagged suites were run with the `os:linux` tag relaxed for the run and restored; the tags in this commit are unchanged.

## Scope

- The web client is unchanged; whether #1205 covers it is an open question for the user, not decided here.
- The memory is per browser profile, the same way the desktop keeps the locale, panel width and (#1204) the approval mode.
1207.head: fix-1205-model-memory
1207.title: feat(desktop): start a new conversation from the model last picked

1208.author: yuanzhou75
1208.body:
Follow-up to #1194 (#1182 and #1187 both closed by it): the three suggestions that were deliberately not pushed onto the approved head.

## What changes

**F1 — the read-only fixture is judged by its own write (`application/test/bootstrap.test.ts`).**
`hostMadeReadOnly` had its `writeFile` and its conditional `rm` inside one `try`, so a failed unlink of a file the host had just created was classified as "read-only". Only the write decides now; the unlink is best effort. It failed loudly rather than passing silently, but the classification was wrong.

**F3 — the writable half runs before the skip (same file).**
`assert.equal(await dirWritable(join(root, "rw")), true)` had moved below the NTFS probe, so on the one platform this suite runs on, a regression that made `dirWritable` answer `false` for a writable directory would have been reported as `# skipped`. It is asserted before the probe again, and only the read-only assertion sits below the skip.

**F2 — the build-only flag is pinned in the contract (`.ci/ci-contract.test.mjs`).**
`/pnpm --dir application dist/` matches with or without `--publish never`, so the publish half of the Windows gate had no contract check while the split half did. The contract now asserts the flag, so a later edit cannot restore electron-builder's implicit publish (the #1187 failure) while the test stays green.

## Validation

On this Windows 11 host (Node v22.23.4), against the exact files pushed:

- `application/test/bootstrap.test.ts`: **34 tests, 32 pass, 0 fail, 2 skipped** — the same two NTFS skips, with the writable assertion now before the probe.
- `.ci/ci-contract.test.mjs`: `Windows distribution gate builds the native Electron installer` passes, including the new `--publish never` assertion (run with that file's `os:linux` tag released for this host; the other failures in the file are unrelated absolute-path assertions that assume Linux and are untouched here).
- Root `tsc -p tsconfig.tests.json --noEmit` is clean for these files through CI's gate.

This is test-only; no product or workflow behaviour changes.
1208.head: fix-1194-review-followups
1208.title: test(application): close the three review suggestions deferred from #1194

1209.author: zhaochen39
1209.body:
This change addresses two nightly gate failures: research-6 could stall while the model repeatedly prepared runtime dependencies and built an evaluator, and the API platform proposal fixture no longer matched the current proposal contract.

## Stabilize the platform proposal fixture
The API unit-test fixture now uses the current `npu_job` mode and exposes `weight` as the editable field, matching the proposal schema used by the platform code.

## Bound the research-6 E2E runtime
The research-6 prompt enables thinking with low effort and directs the agent to use the runtime prepared by the test stack. It explicitly avoids reinstalling pip, downloading dependencies, or constructing a second evaluator, then proceeds directly to `create_evolve_run`. This keeps the real JiuwenSwarm journey within the test runtime boundary and prevents the previous gateway stall.

## Validation
- Targeted API unit test: 3 passed, 0 failed (`services/api/src/bootstrap/platform.test.ts`).
- Real JiuwenSwarm research-6 E2E: 1 passed, 0 failed; the run produced 3 valid PUCT expansions.
- Full `ci:l1`, `ci:ut`, `ci:st`, and `ci:e2e` layers were not run, per the requester instruction to skip local test execution for PR preparation.

## E2E user journeys
PASS — tested SHA `1924b123`.

Scenario: open the Evolve Design journey, start the PUCT search, and wait for the run to produce candidate expansions. Expected outcome: the real JiuwenSwarm run completes without a gateway stall and records valid expansions. Actual outcome: the journey passed with 3 valid expansions; session settings were `thinkingMode=enabled` and `thinkingEffort=low`.

## Release
Release category: release:internal
User impact: CI and test stability only; no production behavior change.
Compatibility and migration: none.

1210.author: zhaochen39
1210.body:
This change addresses the nightly gate failure in research-6 and aligns the evolution proposal contract with the current JSON baseline semantics.

## Preserve proposal scope and direction

- Require a JSON object starting point before accepting `editableFields` for `custom_script` proposals.
- Preserve the confirmed proposal directed scorecard fields when a JSON baseline is evolved through `custom_script`.
- Extend proposal and platform tests to cover module rejection, JSON-scope compatibility, and directed-field preservation.

## Keep the JiuwenSwarm research-6 journey within the prepared runtime

- Keep thinking enabled with low effort and the documented PUCT parameters.
- Allow the agent to read the prepared workspace and design the evaluator through the evolve-design skill.
- Prevent dependency installation, network downloads, ad-hoc shell/Python scoring scripts, and duplicate evaluator implementations; the run declared packages supply `numpy` and `scipy`.
- Keep the bounded partial tool-call stream retry in the model gateway and remove the unused visible tool state. This changes recovery behavior for interrupted model turns.

## Other cleanup

- Remove the duplicate Windows `--publish never` argument already supplied by the current main workflow.

## Validation

- WSL targeted API UT: **101 passed, 0 failed, 0 skipped**.
- Real JiuwenSwarm research-6 E2E: **1 passed, 0 failed**, with **3 valid PUCT expansions**; run settings were `thinking=enabled` and `thinkingEffort=low`.
- Full CI layers were not run locally.

Release category: `release:fix`
## Related issues

Closes #1189
Closes #1188
Closes #1186
Closes #1185
Closes #1184

1212.author: ink999107
1212.body:
The 会话设置 row for 程序演进实验 reused a search whenever the Session already had one. After the
first run it could never reach the create dialog again, so the preflight advice "start again from
the setup dialog" pointed at a surface the UI would not show, and a second search could only be
started by typing an `/evolve-design` command.

The same Session also showed a second, independent problem when the continuation was written as a
plain message ("基于Node #2，继续进化"): the model omitted `allowUnisolated`, because that message
carries no `--allow-direct`. The server does not read the current message: it reads the Session's
**latest** `/evolve-design` command, which did carry the flag, so the run was refused by the
model's reading of the rule, not by the server.

## The settings row always starts a design
`openEvolve` in `apps/desktop/src/App.tsx` now always opens 新建程序演进实验 instead of selecting a
running/newest search. Existing searches stay reachable through their cards in the transcript, and
the composer's draft still rides into the new design's task field. The Composer prop comment follows
the behaviour.

A search that is **still running** holds the form rather than disappearing from it: the server
starts one search per Session (`startProposedRun` refuses a second with "this session already has a
search running"), so the dialog now takes the same `isEvolveRunActive` over `evolve.runs` the panel
uses, and `blocked` names it — the form opens, says a search is running and where its card is, and
leaves 开始设计 disabled. A finished search leaves the form usable, which is the state this change
is about. The new cases in `apps/desktop/e2e/evolve.spec.ts` cover both: a finished search still
gets a usable dialog from the settings row, and a running one still opens the dialog but cannot
start a second search.

## Consent for a continuation started from a plain message
`skills/evolve-design/SKILL.md` and the `allowUnisolated` description in `packages/evolve/src/index.ts`
now scope the consent to the design being continued: what it inherits is the `/evolve-design`
command that started that design, read together with the design it started. That is the Session's
latest command only when the continued design is the newest one — with two designs, the latest
command can belong to the other one — so when that cannot be told the flag is left out and the
server refuses with `unisolated_run_unconfirmed`, telling the user to start the run from the setup
dialog. A checkpoint answer does not replace the command, a plain message is not itself an answer,
and a design that begins from one has no command of its own, so it must not inherit another
design's `--allow-direct`.

## Validation
On this head (`fix/desktop-evolve-second-run` rebased onto `e0983db4`):

- Typecheck: desktop and evolve packages pass.
- Desktop unit tests: 1176/1176 pass (0 failed, 0 skipped).
- Evolve unit tests: 16/16 pass (0 failed, 0 skipped).
- Desktop browser suite (`apps/desktop/e2e`, mocked entry): 154 tests, 150 passed, 4 failed.
  The four also fail on the base commit (`b3ec144e`, the previous main) in a detached worktree with the same
  command, in files this diff does not touch: `boot` "resumes the most recent session", both
  `research-package` cases, and `settings-interactions` "a card opens to the skill's source".
- The repository-wide UT and ST layers were last run on the previous head before the rebase; the
  only packages this head changes are the two above, and both were rerun. That earlier run:
  UT 7707 planned / 7676 executed / 7660 passed / 16 failed, all 16 attributed to this host (14
  pass under a clean `TMPDIR`; the remaining 2 also fail on a pristine `main` worktree in files this
  diff does not touch — bwrap 0.6.1 lacks `--disable-userns`, and `start-stack-lock` cannot
  reproduce its interrupt). ST 63 planned / 63 executed / 62 passed / 1 failed:
  `test/api/evolve-distribution` downloads the pinned Python runtime from GitHub Releases, which
  this host cannot reach.

## Screenshots
Captured from the mocked desktop entry, on a Session whose `session-1` already has a search,
clicking 会话设置 → 程序演进实验.

The "before" pair is the same head with `App.tsx` taken from the base, so the only difference
between the pairs is this change.

<details open>
<summary>zh-CN — before / after (finished search)</summary>

Before: the row opens the existing search's 任务 panel.

![zh before](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/ink999107/sciencediscovery/4a960e901a84a21dbb73f07cbf0f68c838759166/pr-assets/1212/zh-before-run.png)

After: the row opens 新建程序演进实验.

![zh after](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/ink999107/sciencediscovery/4a960e901a84a21dbb73f07cbf0f68c838759166/pr-assets/1212/zh-after-dialog.png)

</details>

<details open>
<summary>en-US — before / after (finished search)</summary>

Before: the row opens the existing search's task panel.

![en before](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/ink999107/sciencediscovery/4a960e901a84a21dbb73f07cbf0f68c838759166/pr-assets/1212/en-before-run.png)

After: the row opens New evolution run.

![en after](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/ink999107/sciencediscovery/4a960e901a84a21dbb73f07cbf0f68c838759166/pr-assets/1212/en-after-dialog.png)

</details>

<details open>
<summary>zh-CN / en-US — a search still running</summary>

The same row with a live search: the dialog opens, names the search and disables 开始设计 / Start
designing.

![zh blocked](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/ink999107/sciencediscovery/d062580abad4534b150a5caa514776f167b00d76/pr-assets/1212/zh-blocked-running.png)

![en blocked](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/ink999107/sciencediscovery/d062580abad4534b150a5caa514776f167b00d76/pr-assets/1212/en-blocked-running.png)

</details>

## E2E user journeys
The change is observed on the desktop browser entry. The repository-wide mocked journeys were
not rerun on this head: nothing in them reaches the settings row or the create dialog, and the
server-side consent check is unchanged.

- `apps/desktop/e2e/evolve.spec.ts` — 16/16 passed, including "the settings row starts a new design
  when the session's search has finished" and "the settings row still opens the create dialog while
  a search runs, and says why it cannot start".
- Full desktop suite — 154 tests, 150 passed, 4 failed, all four pre-existing on the base (above).
- No API, CLI or local-stack journey exercises this surface: the change is the desktop dialog's
  entry and its blocked copy. The server-side consent check it describes is unchanged.

## Release
Release category: release:fix
User impact: the 程序演进实验 row in 会话设置 now always opens the create dialog, so a second
experiment can be started from the UI without typing a command; while a search is live the dialog
says so instead of offering a start the server would refuse; and a continuation started from a
plain message can carry the no-isolation consent the user already gave.
Compatibility and migration: none.

1213.author: ink999107
1213.body:
The desktop front end had no Reviewer Specialist surface. The service writes a
review for every artifact it audits — a `reviewer_checkpoint` message in the
transcript plus an `ArtifactReviewRun` — and the desktop read neither, so a
Session could be reviewed at the Quick or Deep level with nothing on screen to
say what the review concluded.

## The verdict card

A checkpoint message now draws a card in the conversation, joined to its
reviews by `toolCallId`, so the verdict sits under the turn that produced the
artifact rather than at the end of the Session. One checkpoint can cover
several artifacts and each gets its own framed section, titled with its
artifact's logical name and carrying that artifact's own verdict; the header
reports the worst of them and adds "N 通过 · M 需处理" when they disagree.

The colour states what there is to trust:

- **red** — a problem with the artifact: any finding, or delivery checked and
  incomplete;
- **amber** — the verdict itself is not current: the review failed, or the
  artifact has a newer version and the verdict is history;
- **grey** — nothing was found, but nothing was confirmed either: the
  checkpoint was skipped, it produced no review, delivery was never verified,
  or the review itself declared a check it did not run;
- **green** — the level ran, raised nothing, and delivery was confirmed — or
  the review was structure-only and never claimed any delivery verdict.

`unverifiedDelivery` is a port of the server's own `reviewUnverifiedDelivery`,
and `declaredGap` of `reviewDeclaredGap` — the rule the web client already uses
to keep a partial review out of its "passed" count. A review whose record lists
an unchecked item used to read "未发现问题", green, while its own rows below said
"未检查" for the same item; it now reads "未发现问题，但有 N 项未检查", grey.

The desktop cannot import the schema's runtime (its barrel reaches a JSON
property import), so each rule is one copy with the server's tests behind it
rather than a second, drifting reading.

Expanding a card shows findings first, then the delivery verdict, then the
checks that ran, then what the review could not do. A source verdict keeps the
claim it answers for and the reviewer's account, with the locator count when a
passage was found; a source service that returned no conclusion is rendered as
"来源核验没有得出结论" and the service's raw error text is not printed: it is
not a finding about the report. A citation lookup that reached no conclusion is
not drawn as a row of its own — a row saying "无结论" beside a citation-format
pass reads as the card contradicting itself — and what the review could not do
is still said once, as the `claim_support` gap it declares.

Each check-category label and the level pill carry their explanation as a hover
title, and the level pill only names the level (快速 / 深度).

## A running review says where it is

A checkpoint in flight draws a running line instead of a verdict. It names the
coordinator's `phase` (`quick`, `preparing`, `computation`, `citation`), counts
what is finished against what there is, names the artifact in hand and how many
checks are queued, and draws a thin progress track under the line. When the
coordinator has not said how much there is, the bar is not drawn and the line
stays generic rather than showing a 0/0 that looks like a stall.

## The Session can ask for a review

会话设置 gains 立即审查 / 停止审查, next to the automatic-review switch and the
level. That switch decides whether a review happens by itself; this row is the
reader asking for one now, so it stays enabled when automatic review is off.
审查档位 stays open for the same reason: the coordinator reads the Session's
level for a manual run too (`enqueueManual` uses `sessionSettings.level`).

The click has to look like something happened immediately, so the client mints
a checkpoint message id, `POST …/reviewer-specialist/review` answers with the
queued `task`, and the running card is drawn into the transcript at once. The
server's copy replaces it when the queue empties and one `GET` of the Session
converges the transcript; an automatic review, which publishes no event at this
window, is surfaced by the same read once the queue empties. A re-run mints a
new checkpoint instead of reusing the one it was pressed on: the store refuses
an existing message id whose tool call id belongs to another task. 停止审查
calls `POST …/reviewer-specialist/cancel` and reports the server's answer; a
409 is shown as an error rather than a silent no-op.

## The artifact dialog's 审查 tab

The version on screen gets its own tab with the same rows; when the version is
no longer current the verdict is marked as history and a re-run is offered. The
re-run names a fresh checkpoint message id and follows the task it queued.

## Settings

设置 › 专家 lists the Review Specialist as a built-in card — 审查, with the one
line 由自动审阅使用 — and nothing on that page can switch it off, the shape the
reference client uses. The composer's settings menu carries the Session's
automatic review and level. The server's system-wide setting is still read on
Session load and on each reviewer refresh (another client can have turned it
off); when it is off the Session's switch is disabled and the menu says why. The
desktop no longer writes that setting.

## Validation

Desktop layers on this head:

| Layer | Result |
| --- | --- |
| `apps/desktop` unit (`npm test`) | 1433 passed / 0 failed |
| `apps/desktop` typecheck (`npm run typecheck`) | clean |
| Reviewer browser spec (`apps/desktop/e2e/reviewer.spec.ts`) | 14 passed / 0 failed |
| Desktop browser suite (`apps/desktop/e2e`) | 174 passed / 0 failed / 0 skipped (run locally; not a CI job) |

The repo-wide UT, ST and mocked E2E layers run in CI on this head. The desktop
browser suite is not part of the CI gate — it was run locally on this head —
and the `smart` level is rendered as Deep, matching the web client.

## E2E user journeys

PASS on the desktop browser entry (mocked per-page API; no backend), run locally on this head:

- a confirmed delivery is green and its checks are one press away;
- a checkpoint over two artifacts names both in separate framed sections, each
  carrying its own verdict while the header reports the worse one;
- a review that never verified delivery is grey, not green;
- a review that declared an unchecked item is grey and named;
- structure-only is green because it never claimed delivery;
- an incomplete delivery is red;
- a stale verdict says it is history and offers a re-run that names a fresh
  checkpoint;
- the eight-checkpoint Quick/Deep outcome matrix, including the two skip
  reasons and a reload;
- a running review reporting its phase and progress;
- an automatic review's card arriving on its own when the coordinator finishes;
- 立即审查 with automatic review off, at a level chosen while that switch is
  off; 停止审查 stopping one already under way;
- a reviewer switched off on the server disabling the Session switch with its
  explanation;
- the built-in Review expert listed on 专家 with no switch;
- the artifact dialog's 审查 tab queueing a re-run with a fresh message id.

The shared `test/journey-reviewer-*.spec.ts` journeys run in the mocked E2E
layer against the real control plane; CI reports them on this head.

Closes #1203 — the desktop Reviewer Specialist feature request this implements.

## Release

Release category: `release:feature` (the GitHub label is pending a maintainer: this account has no write access to apply it)
User impact: the desktop app shows Reviewer Specialist verdicts, can run or stop
a review from the Session settings, and configures both Reviewer settings
layers.
Compatibility and migration: none. No API or configuration change.

1215.author: ink999107
1215.body: Closes #1199. ## What changes The desktop 设置 › 技能 page gains the surfaces the web app has and the desktop did not: importing a Skill, editing one in place, reading one on its own page, and taking a package back out. Import, edit, and detail are pages inside the settings pane rather than dialogs, so the list stays one step away. - **添加技能** is a menu in the list header with three entries: **上传技能** (a `SKILL.md`, a ZIP package, or a `.skill` archive, dropped or picked), **从 GitHub 导入** (inspect the repository, then pick the packages to install), and **从零开始写** (the existing authored form). - **搜索** narrows the list on a Skill's name or description as the user types. The global switches stay above the filtered rows and still act on the whole list; a term that matches nothing says so instead of leaving the page blank. - A repository is inspected first (`POST /api/skills/import-git/inspect`) and each chosen package is imported at the commit that inspection saw, so what the user reviewed is what gets installed. Replacing an installed Skill requires `overwrite` plus the revision the user saw (`expectedRevision`); a different revision is a 409 rather than a silent replacement of an edit made in another window. Re-importing identical bytes is a no-op instead of an empty revision, and a built-in Skill stays read-only. - An inspection of a real, large repository says what it is doing and offers **取消**, which stops waiting without reporting a failure. The metadata clone has a 60 s ceiling and the checkout that fetches files 180 s; a timeout is reported as one. The scan no longer downloads the repository: it clones commit metadata only (`--filter=blob:none`) and checks out just the `SKILL.md` files (non-cone sparse), which is what discovery and the candidate list read. A package's resources are fetched only when an installed Skill has to be compared (unchanged vs update) or when the package is imported. A server without partial-clone support falls back to a plain shallow clone — and only an explicit refusal of the filter falls back: previously any transport error did, which turned a one-second hiccup into a 471 MB download (`github.com/k-dense-ai/scientific-agent-skills`) and made a normally 4 s inspection time out at 180 s. A transfer that broke (early EOF, `RPC failed`, reset connection, TLS) is now retried as the same clone once, and a transfer that stops moving is abandoned after 30 s below 1 KiB/s. - The checkout an inspection made is kept for 15 minutes, so the packages that follow are imported from it instead of cloning the repository once per package. Measured against `github.com/k-dense-ai/scientific-agent-skills` (~471 MB, 177 `SKILL.md` files): inspection went from 29 s to **3.6 s** through the API (0.07 s to import a package whose content is its `SKILL.md` alone, 1.1 s for one with 15 resource files). Before the checkout was reused, an import spent ~41 s cloning on its own. A request for another commit, ref or repository still clones. - A selection is imported by one **background job** (`POST /api/skills/import-git/jobs`). The page returns to the list as soon as the job is accepted; the list reports `正在后台导入 n / total`, and the job keeps going when the reader leaves 设置. The job expands the retained checkout once for the whole selection instead of once per package, reports per-package failures without stopping the rest, and switches on the packages it created when JiuwenSwarm is the backend. A job the server no longer knows (a restart or its 30-minute cleanup) is treated as terminal instead of being polled forever. Same-name uploads are renamed only when the desktop asks; the route's default remains 409. - Discovery used to stop at 100 packages, which silently hid 77 of that repository's 177; discovery now lists every package the checkout holds, so no repository can be silently truncated. One inspection response carries at most **500** candidates, reports the repository's `total`, and returns a `nextCursor` while more remain. **加载更多** reads the next page at the same commit, from the checkout the first page made (no second clone); the rows already read stay on screen with their ticks, and new importable rows join the selection only when the user had kept everything selected. Candidate cards use `content-visibility: auto`, so a response holding hundreds of them costs what is on screen. Against the same repository one page is enough: 177 candidates, `total` 177, no cursor. - **Clicking a Skill opens the Skill's own page**, as OpenScience does, instead of expanding its instructions inside the card. A breadcrumb names the list, and the page carries the Skill's mark, name and source badge above its description, **文件** with `SKILL.md` rendered in a measured column, and **详情** printing the frontmatter keys the package declares (`许可证`, `allowed-tools`, `compatibility`, …) as label-over-value facts, omitted entirely when there are none. At the product owner's request the page does not repeat the list's switch, a version line, or a 可用范围 block: availability is a list decision, and repeating it here only pushed the document down the page. Sections are separated by a hairline rather than boxed in cards; the instruction column is `minmax(0, 1fr)`, so a wide table scrolls inside the prose instead of stretching the page. - A row ends in a chevron. Hovering it opens the actions that package allows, drawn in the row's own popover and flipped upwards when the row sits near the bottom of the pane: **导出** on every package (a built-in is read-only, not uncopyable), and **编辑** / **删除** on a managed package: - **导出** downloads the installed package as the ZIP the importer accepts back (`GET /api/skills/:id/package`, built by `SkillCatalog.exportPackage` from the same files the importer reads, under the single root directory an uploaded package has), so an export can be imported again here or on another machine without rearranging it. Built-in packages export too: read-only says who may change them, not who may copy them. - **编辑** opens the editor below. - **删除** reads the deletion impact first (`GET /api/skills/:id/deletion-impact`); if a Project or Session selection still names the package it says how many and stops, rather than turning the route's refusal into a failed request. Otherwise the deletion goes through the settings shell's one confirmation dialog, which names the Skill and what removing it means. - **编辑** is a page of its own: name (read-only), description, one content editor with 撰写 / 上传, and a collapsed 高级设置 holding license, compatibility and the package's files. Reference files can be added under a chosen subdirectory (`references`, `assets`, `scripts`, …); choosing one opens an editor under its row with its own 保存文件, while the main editor stays `SKILL.md`. A non-UTF-8 pick is refused before any write. Saving sends back `metadata` and `allowed-tools` as declared (string or YAML sequence), so optional frontmatter is not dropped; a stale revision from another window surfaces as a conflict message. A partial multi-file upload still surfaces the revision it already stored. - **Uploading a package whose name is taken** is the desktop's choice, not a change to the route's contract: the desktop sends `onDuplicate=rename`, and the server installs it as `name-2`, `name-3`, … with `SKILL.md`'s name rewritten. `POST /api/skills/import` keeps its historical 409 for web and CLI callers, which omit the flag. Every page below the list replaces it and is left through the header's back control; the editor also offers 取消 in its footer, which is the same exit. The header names the page that is actually open, and the list keeps the installed count. The pages share one content measure so moving between them does not move the fields under the pointer, and they reuse the pane's existing tokens and controls rather than introducing a second visual language. A newly installed Skill is enabled when the switches are available; the background job owns that step, so closing 设置 before it finishes does not skip it. Updating an already-installed Skill leaves its switch alone, because a user may have switched it off on purpose. Closing 设置 after visiting 技能 re-reads the catalog, so the composer's `/` palette reflects the change without a reload. Backend support: `ImportSkillFromGitRequest` gains optional `commit`, `overwrite` and `expectedRevision`; `InspectGitSkillRepositoryRequest` gains optional `commit` and `cursor`, and `GitSkillRepositoryInspection` gains `total` and `nextCursor`; background imports add `StartGitSkillImportJobRequest` and `GitSkillImportJob` with `POST/GET /api/skills/import-git/jobs`; `CreateSkillRequest.allowedTools` accepts `string | string[]`; `SkillCatalog` accepts an injectable checkout so the Git import branches can be tested without a network; `SkillCatalog.exportPackage` builds an installed package as a ZIP and `GET /api/skills/:id/package` serves it as `application/zip` with a `content-disposition` name; and `SKILL_VALIDATION` now maps to HTTP 400 instead of falling through to an unclassified 500 when its message wording does not match the client-input patterns. ## Screenshots Captured at `308c08e1`, 1440×900, in zh-CN and en; the list images (`01`, `02`) and the search images were refreshed at `867b4ebb`, where the search field sits above the list. The save dialog is a native OS window, so a page screenshot cannot capture it; the export image shows the row after the write, and the E2E stubs the picker to assert the ZIP name and bytes. The detail page intentionally has no 可用范围 block, version line or switch: those were removed at the product owner's request, and availability stays in the list. | State | 中文 | English | |---|---|---| | 技能 list + 添加技能 menu | | | | Row chevron menu (导出 / 编辑 / 删除) | | | | 上传技能 | | | | Skill detail | | | | 编辑 | | | | Edit-save conflict | | | | 删除 confirmation | | | | Delete refused while a selection names it | | | | 导出 result (native dialog not page-capturable) | | | | 从 GitHub 导入 — inspection running | | | | Git candidates with ticks | | | | Git candidates after 加载更多 | | | | 技能 search filtering the list | | | | A term that matches nothing | | | | Search at 1100 px (no horizontal overflow) | | | ## What was run ### Search and rebase (`867b4ebb`) - Rebased onto `main` (`0c3d4d52`); the merge queue had rejected the previous head as conflicting after #1258. No merge commit: the 25 branch commits were replayed on the new base. - `pnpm --filter @sciencediscovery/desktop typecheck` — pass - `apps/desktop` unit tests — 1277 pass, 0 fail (adds the search field: typing a term narrows both lists, and a term with no match renders the no-match line instead of the empty state) - Desktop Vite against the live stack at 1440×900 and 1100 px, zh-CN and en: the field renders above the list, filtering matches name and description, the no-match line appears, and the pane has no horizontal overflow. ### After the review round (`308c08e1`) - `pnpm --filter @sciencediscovery/desktop typecheck` — pass - `apps/desktop` skill suites — 70 pass; background-job store tests — 2 pass - `services/api` skills + import-job tests — 27 pass - full desktop Skill E2E journey — 1 passed (13.0 s) - `pnpm --recursive typecheck` — pass (all workspace packages) - `tsc -p tsconfig.tests.json` — pass - `apps/desktop` unit tests — 1193 pass, 0 fail (includes a two-page repository: the header shows the repository total, 加载更多 reads at the same commit from the returned cursor, the rows already read stay, and loading more does not re-tick a selection the user cleared; the card opens the detail page and lists what the page must show; the chevron menu offers 导出 / 编辑 / 删除 only on a managed row, closes on Escape and on a press outside, exports the returned bytes, deletes through the confirmation dialog, and reports a package still named by a selection instead of deleting it) - `packages/specialist` unit tests — 10 pass, 0 fail. Four drive the real checkout against a `git` on `PATH` that answers like the transport: a broken transfer retries the same clone and never asks for a full repository, a clone that never answers is attempted again before giving up, a checkout that loses its connection is fetched again, a refused filter is the only path to a full clone, and a repository that does not exist is cloned exactly once. - `services/api` Skill suites (`skills.test.ts`, `skills-git-import.test.ts`) — 30 pass, 0 fail (includes the checkout-reuse case, a partial-checkout case that builds a real sparse clone from a local repository and asserts that the resources are fetched on import and that the second scan reports `unchanged`, a 120-package listing, a 520-package repository read as 500 + 20 from one checkout with no gap or overlap, a cursor without its commit rejected, `exportPackage` opening its own archive with the importer's unzip — the files under the Skill's root directory, the same bytes importing back through the upload path, a read-only built-in exporting, and an unknown id refused — and the lifecycle test downloading `/api/skills/:id/package` and checking `application/zip`, the `content-disposition` name, the archive's entries, and a 404 for a Skill that does not exist) - `services/api` targeted suites (`server.test.ts`, `skills.test.ts`) — 138 run, 135 pass. The 3 failures are pre-existing and environmental: `services/paper/.venv` is absent in this checkout (PDF upload test), and two subagent event-order assertions expecting a `model.usage` event that this host does not emit; both fail without this change. - `node test/check-e2e-meta.mjs` — 96 spec files, 0 errors - `pnpm docs:lint` — 0 issues - Live stack: `POST /api/skills/import-git/inspect` against `github.com/k-dense-ai/scientific-agent-skills` returned 177 candidates with `total` 177 and no cursor; importing one package took 0.07 s. The desktop (Vite on 4178, 1440×900) drew all 177 rows and showed no 加载更多, because that repository fits in one page. The inspection ran in 4.2 s when the network answered, and 64 s instead of a 180 s failure when the first clone was cut at the new ceiling and the retry answered. ## E2E `test/journey-desktop-skill-import-edit.spec.ts` (mocked, zh-CN, desktop Vite entry on 4178 against an isolated stack on 4510): 8 steps pass. 1216.author: yuanzhou75
1216.body:
Closes #1211

#1211 lists six findings from the #1200 review that the 5 GiB default exposed. This PR fixes all six, on the server, in the package library, and in both clients that save the archive.

## What changed, per finding

**F1 — the restore no longer holds a whole session's workspace objects.** `services/api/src/research-snapshots.ts` now collects the workspace `objectPath` list first (`workspaceEntries`) and looks each object up inside the write loop, so the peak is one object instead of the sum of the session's workspace. An object missing from the unpacked directory is recorded as an omission and the restore continues, which is what the memory requirement in `http/index.ts` already assumed.

**F2 — the 5 GiB default only reaches paths that stream.**
- Server: the synchronous `GET …/research-package` route now pre-flights the export on `archiveBytes` *before* writing headers (a refusal after `writeHead` can only truncate the body), builds the input with `streamObjects`, drops `content-length`, and writes tar → gzip straight into the response via `writeResearchPackage`; a failed write destroys the response instead of claiming success.
- Web: `exportResearchPackage` returns the live `Response` instead of `response.blob()`. New `apps/web/src/research-package/save-stream.ts` opens `showSaveFilePicker` *inside the click* — the picker needs the transient user activation that a `fetch` round trip would consume — then pipes `response.body` into the writable; a failed export aborts it so no partial file survives, and a cancelled dialog returns without closing the dialog or exporting anything.
- Desktop + shell: new `export-stream-begin/chunk/end/abort` IPC channels (`application/src/export-sink.ts`, `main.ts`, `preload.ts`) keep one file descriptor per destination token and append each chunk. The stream writes a sibling `<destination>.<token>.part` and `streamEnd` renames it onto the destination only after the close succeeds, so a save that fails at 80% - or a renderer that disappears - leaves the archive the user already had untouched; `abort`/`abortAll` remove the temporary only, a zero-byte stream is dropped instead of published, and a reused live token aborts the previous stream rather than committing it. The durable history row is written at `streamEnd` with the size the stream actually wrote, so it keeps the behaviour the whole-buffer `write` had. `apps/desktop` forwards `response.body` chunk by chunk and only falls back to the one-shot `write` on a shell that lacks the channels; a plain browser still falls back to the anchor download.
- Two client paths still buffer, and both are named here rather than implied away: a browser without the File System Access API keeps the old whole-blob download, and the background-export download (`downloadResearchPackageExport` → `downloadBlob`) runs in a completion poll, outside any user activation, so it cannot open the file picker and still takes `response.blob()`. Moving that one to a destination picked when the user starts the export is the follow-up, not part of #1211's six findings.

**F3 — a write error during a streamed import rejects instead of killing the process.** The object write races against `new Promise((_, reject) => file.on("error", reject))` and the catch destroys the file, so an `EEXIST` open or a late flush error rejects the import instead of becoming an unhandled `'error'` event.

**F5 — each check now charges only what it will still write.** `researchPackageRestoreRequirement` charges `unpacked * 3 + records` (snapshot objects, version blobs and workspace files — the three copies a restore writes), `researchPackageUnpackBudget` is `free / 4` so that a package the unpack step admits cannot be refused by the post-parse check on the same volume, and the export requirement charges the archive it writes (`bytes`) rather than the copies a restore adds. `researchPackageBudgetRefusal` quotes the same 3× figure it refuses on. The new case runs the two halves together — 16 GiB free, 3.8 GiB package — which is the pairing that was missing: each half passed alone and the pair still refused.

**F6 — trailing bytes after the tar terminator no longer hang the import.** `ChunkQueue.drain()` was added: after the zero block the decompressor is drained to completion, and non-zero trailing bytes are refused with `Research package carries data after its end` instead of parking the sink in `offer` forever.

**F7 — a missing CAS blob becomes an omission instead of a failed export.** `addObjectSource` is async and checks `provenanceRecorder.cas.has(hash)` before enqueueing the lazy source; a missing blob pushes `cas:<hash>:unavailable source object` into `omissions` and is left out of the inventory, matching the resident read path.

## This import bound is deliberately stricter than `main`

`main` charges a restore `unpacked * 2 + records` and gives the parse `free / 3`, which is consistent with itself: `2 x free/3` is the two thirds that remain after the tree is written. This branch charges `unpacked * 3 + records` (F5 adds the workspace files and one version blob per object, which were never counted) and therefore gives the parse `free / 4`, so `3 x free/4` is exactly the three quarters that remain.

The consequence is a real behaviour change, and it should not be read as a slowdown or a regression:

- **With 12 GiB free, `main` accepts a 4 GiB unpacked package; this head accepts up to 3 GiB.** The fourth GiB is what the restore would need on top of the tree.
- The post-parse restore check moved from `2x` to `3x` for the same reason.
- **A package that imported before can now be refused before it is written** — refused rather than expanded and then abandoned, which is what happened without the workspace files in the count: the parse filled up to a quarter of the volume and the restore failed afterwards, leaving nothing.

That is the cost F5 pays on purpose. The refusal is early and it names what is missing; it is not a performance change and the saved archive format is untouched.

## The browser export saves through the file picker

On the web app the foreground export now streams the archive into the File System
Access picker (`apps/web/src/research-package/save-stream.ts`) instead of buffering
it into a download; that is what keeps a multi-GiB package out of memory. Browsers
without that API keep the previous anchor download, and the background export still
buffers a blob (`ResearchPackageExportTasks`), so it is unchanged.

The mocked journey that reads the exported bytes cannot drive a native save dialog,
which is why the merge group for this head failed (`waitForEvent("download")`
timed out in `journey-restore-research.spec.ts`). That journey now takes the picker
away and asserts the fallback, and the streaming path keeps its own coverage in
`apps/web/tests/save-stream.test.ts`.

## Verification

Local, Windows 11 + Node 22.23.4. Tests that carry `os:linux` were run with the tag removed and then restored, and `node:test` skips are not counted as passes.

- `packages/research-package` `stream-import.test.ts`: **9/9** — including 20 MiB of trailing zeros completing, non-zero trailing bytes refused, and a `EEXIST` write error rejecting the import.
- `services/api` `research-package-preflight.test.ts`: **18/18** — including "an export is charged the archive it writes, not the copies a restore adds", "a restore is charged only the copies it still has to write" and "the unpack budget and the post-parse check agree on the same free disk".
- `services/api` `research-package-http.test.ts`: **23/23**.
- `services/api` `research-package-exports.test.ts`: **9/9**.
- Web: new `save-stream.test.ts` **4/4** (a two-chunk body arrives as two writes, which fails if the caller buffers first; picker cancel starts no request; a failed export aborts; no picker still downloads) and `ResearchPackageActions.test.tsx` **5/5**.
- Desktop: `export-bridge-stream.test.ts` **3/3**, `research-package.test.ts` **6/6**, and the view suite `research-package-export-ack` 1/1, `research-package-export-session` **2/2** (the new case asserts `begin → chunk → chunk → end` and that the one-shot `write` is *not* used), `research-package-trim` 5/5.
- Shell: `application/test/export-sink.test.ts` **4/4**, plus the existing `export-tokens` and `export-history` suites **12/12**.
- `tsc --noEmit`: `apps/web`, `apps/desktop` and the root `tsconfig.tests.json` are clean.
- Mutation checks: restoring the whole-buffer `arrayBuffer()` write in the web sink turns the new web case red; short-circuiting the desktop streaming branch onto the one-shot `write` turns the new view case red; both were reverted.

## What was not run locally

- `application` (the Electron shell) has no `node_modules` on this machine, so `tsc -p application/tsconfig.json` cannot run here; the shell is covered by its unit tests above and by CI, and I have not run it in a real Electron window.
- No end-to-end save of a multi-GiB package through a real browser or shell was performed here. The 5 GiB server-side numbers are the ones measured for #1200 (`merge-group` run `44079501355`), and the client halves are covered by chunk-level assertions, not by a real 5 GiB transfer.

## Screenshots

Desktop shell (vite dev + the repository's `e2e/fixtures` control plane, `window.sdShell` stubbed), 1440×900, zh-CN and en. Each capture is backed by a DOM assertion, not just a picture.

| state | zh-CN | en |
| --- | --- | --- |
| dialog open, nothing started | ![zh idle](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/yuanzhou75/sciencediscovery/screenshots-1216/docs/screenshots/1216/1216-desktop-zh-CN-idle.png) | ![en idle](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/yuanzhou75/sciencediscovery/screenshots-1216/docs/screenshots/1216/1216-desktop-en-idle.png) |
| saved: 证据包已保存 / Package saved | ![zh saved](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/yuanzhou75/sciencediscovery/screenshots-1216/docs/screenshots/1216/1216-desktop-zh-CN-saved.png) | ![en saved](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/yuanzhou75/sciencediscovery/screenshots-1216/docs/screenshots/1216/1216-desktop-en-saved.png) |
| saving: 1 个导出进行中 / 1 export in progress (sidebar row) | ![zh saving](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/yuanzhou75/sciencediscovery/screenshots-1216/docs/screenshots/1216/1216-desktop-zh-CN-saving.png) | ![en saving](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/yuanzhou75/sciencediscovery/screenshots-1216/docs/screenshots/1216/1216-desktop-en-saving.png) |
| cancelled: the dialog stays open, nothing started | ![zh cancelled](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/yuanzhou75/sciencediscovery/screenshots-1216/docs/screenshots/1216/1216-desktop-zh-CN-cancelled.png) | ![en cancelled](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/yuanzhou75/sciencediscovery/screenshots-1216/docs/screenshots/1216/1216-desktop-en-cancelled.png) |
| failed: 保存证据包失败 / Failed to save the package | ![zh failed](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/yuanzhou75/sciencediscovery/screenshots-1216/docs/screenshots/1216/1216-desktop-zh-CN-failed.png) | ![en failed](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/yuanzhou75/sciencediscovery/screenshots-1216/docs/screenshots/1216/1216-desktop-en-failed.png) |

What each state pins: `idle` shows the dialog with its size estimate; `saved` shows the success line after a streamed save (`1` chunk crossed the bridge); `saving` shows the sidebar row while the body is still arriving; `cancelled` shows the dialog still open with nothing started and no chunks written — cancelling the native save dialog is silent by design, which is stated here rather than implied away; `failed` shows the failure line when the shell's write rejects.

**web**: not captured. Driving the web app's session menu to the export dialog did not reach the dialog in this harness — `onSelect` runs, but `App.tsx:5217` only opens it when `activeProjectId` is set, and that state stayed empty under the mocked control plane. Rather than fake a screen, this PR records the gap: the web save path itself is covered by `apps/web/tests/save-stream.test.ts` (4/4: two-chunk body, picker cancel, failed export abort, no-picker fallback).


## Web client, same dialog

The web save path is the other surface this PR changes (`apps/web/src/research-package/save-stream.ts`, `ResearchPackageActions.tsx`): the picker opens before the request, an aborted picker writes nothing, and a failed write reports itself in the dialog instead of closing as if it had saved. Captured in the web client (Vite dev at `apps/web`, mock control plane, 1440×900), zh-CN and en, with the dialog text asserted at capture time:

| state | assertion at capture time |
| --- | --- |
| idle | dialog open, `取消 / Cancel` + `后台导出 / Background export` + `立即导出 / Immediate export` |
| saved | picker + writable accept every chunk, `close()` resolves → dialog closes: `(dialog closed after the save)` |
| saving | the body is still arriving → primary button reads `处理中… / Processing…` |
| cancelled | picker rejects with `AbortError` → dialog stays, nothing written |
| failed | `write()` rejects → dialog stays and shows `磁盘已满：无法写入证据包` above the buttons |

**Route in a real build** (the screenshots are the dialog itself, not the whole page): open the Project in the sidebar, pick the Session row's `⋯` menu → `导出` (Export) → `导出证据包` (Export evidence package). The dialog only opens when a Project is selected — the sidebar row is what sets `activeProjectId` (`App.tsx:5217`), which is why driving the session menu alone shows nothing.

1217.author: qingkwl
1217.body:
Three macOS release-chain follow-ups from the acceptance review (issue #1165). Based on latest main (`b2075e49`); none of the 24 commits since PR #1156 touched these two files (verified by blob sha). Head is now `0ce130c3` (three stacked follow-ups on the original three changes, see commit list).

## 1. 5f gate: blockmap assertion missed electron-builder 26.x naming

The M4 clean-room signed build (`0.4.0`, builder `26.15.3`) produced a **healthy** differential-update asset, but the 5f manifest gate failed to find it:

| builder | blockmap name |
|---|---|
| 25.x | `ScienceDiscovery-…-mac-arm64.blockmap` (replaces `.zip`) |
| 26.x | `ScienceDiscovery-…-mac-arm64.zip.blockmap` (appends to full name) |

The gate asserted the 25.x name only. Fix: gate like the DMG/zip discovery — **exactly one** of the two names may exist (0 or 2 candidates fail the gate), so a stale same-version blockmap left under the other naming cannot silently ship differential data that does not match the zip (review F1):

```bash
BLOCKMAP=""
FOUND=0
for candidate in "${ZIP}.blockmap" "${ZIP%.zip}.blockmap"; do
  if [ -f "$candidate" ]; then
    BLOCKMAP="$candidate"
    FOUND=$((FOUND + 1))
  fi
done
if [ "$FOUND" -eq 2 ]; then
  die "… BOTH … a stale same-version blockmap … clean release/ and rerun"
elif [ "$FOUND" -eq 0 ]; then
  die "… the differential-update data was not written; rerun electron-builder (zip target)"
fi
```

(FOUND=0 and FOUND=2 carry separate messages — review F2: the shared line told the operator to clean `release/` even when nothing stale existed.)

## 2. 5f gate: uninstaller is not a gated release asset (F4)

`application/scripts/uninstall-mac.command` is the supported macOS removal path (review F4: a macOS user who wants out — or hits a broken install — has no other removal path), but the 5f manifest never gated or listed it. Now:

- gated as the **fifth** asset: `missing scripts/uninstall-mac.command` fails the gate;
- listed in the printed manifest;
- appended to the printed `gh release create` command.

(Path correction vs. the PR #1156 merge description: the script lives at `application/scripts/uninstall-mac.command`, not repo-root `scripts/`.)

## 3. `minimumSystemVersion: 14.0.0` (acceptance ⑦)

Decision basis:
- Electron 37 upstream supports the last 3 macOS majors; macOS 13 (Ventura) has fallen outside that window — no test coverage, no Gatekeeper data;
- our only real acceptance machine runs 14.8.9;
- pinning it here writes `LSMinimumSystemVersion` into Info.plist so Gatekeeper enforces the floor at install/first-run instead of documentation.

## Verification

- `bash -n application/scripts/build-mac.sh` — clean
- `js-yaml` parse of `electron-builder.yml` — `mac.minimumSystemVersion = 14.0.0`, all mac keys intact
- exactly-one probe tested on all three paths: 1 candidate hits (real 26.x artifacts, `…zip.blockmap`, 674,136 bytes), 2 candidates rejected, 0 rejected — with the split messages landing on the right branch
- remote blob shas match local `git hash-object` byte-for-byte at every push (`46cfca97`/`d5603224` → `2516b9e0` → `651eca21`)

Part of issue #1165 (items ⑦ + bot F4 + the 26.x blockmap fix found while producing the M4 release build; review F1/F2 follow-ups folded in).

1219.author: yuanzhou75
1219.body:
Closes #1218

## Why

`assemble` discovered that the JiuwenSwarm venv no longer matched the swarm patch set only inside "verifying payload imports", i.e. after the backend tree, the venv template, micromamba and the bytecode precompile had all been written — 759 s on the run the issue cites. The refusal was right, the timing was not: the same run succeeds in 835 s after `node scripts/jiuwenswarm.mjs setup`, so every dependency-carrying patch cost a full payload assembly to learn about.

## What changes

**A lockfile-driven preflight at the start of `assemble`, before any payload write.** `application/scripts/lib/venv-lock-consistency.mjs` reads the *patched* `data/jiuwenswarm/src/uv.lock`, asks the jw venv once for every installed distribution (`importlib.metadata` in a single python call) and reports each package whose installed version differs from the pin. `assemble-backend.mjs` runs it right after the stale-dist gate and **before `rm(out)`/`mkdir(out)`**, so a stale venv costs seconds and leaves `build/resources` untouched.

**It is generic, not greenlet-specific.** 0018-desktop-slim-deps, 0019-align-workspace-versions and 0021-greenlet-static-runtime all rewrite `pyproject.toml`/`uv.lock`; whatever a future patch pins is checked without touching this code. Packages the lock lists for other platforms or optional groups are ignored when the venv does not install them — the direction this exists for is an installed package lagging its patched pin.

**The end-of-run gate stays.** The greenlet MSVC140/native-import gate is untouched and still runs as the second line of defence (a venv can, in principle, change mid-run).

The refusal names both versions and the same repair command the end gate uses:

```
[assemble] FAIL: jw venv preflight FAILED: the venv does not match the swarm patch set:
pip 25.0.1 (uv.lock requires 0.0.1). A dependency-carrying patch rewrote the lockfile but
the venv predates it. Re-run node scripts/jiuwenswarm.mjs setup (or bash scripts/jiuwenswarm.sh setup), then rebuild.
```

## Proof that the refusal happens before the payload is written

A real `assemble` run against a fixture whose lock pins `pip` differently from its venv (the same shape as greenlet 3.5.0 vs 3.5.5):

```
[assemble] sanity checks passed
[assemble] stale-dist gate passed (services/packages/apps)
[assemble] FAIL: jw venv preflight FAILED: ... pip 25.0.1 (uv.lock requires 0.0.1) ...
exit=1  elapsed=516 ms  out exists: False
```

- **516 ms**, against the 759 s the issue measured for the same discovery at the end gate.
- **`--out` was never created**: the preflight runs before `rm(out)`/`mkdir(out)`, so there is no payload to leave half-written. The check is asserted by a test as well (`the preflight runs before assemble writes anything`) so a future edit cannot move it back below the copy steps.
- With a lock that matches its venv, the same fixture prints `jw venv matches the swarm patch set's uv.lock` and proceeds to the deploy step — the check does not fire on a correct tree.

## Tests

- `application/test/assemble-venv-preflight.test.ts` (new): parses `[[package]]` pins; reports a stale installed version and not the pin; ignores a locked package the venv does not install; no refusal when they agree; the message names both versions and both setup commands; the skew list is bounded; and the ordering pin above.
- `pnpm --dir application test`: **352 tests, 348 pass, 0 fail, 4 skipped** (the skips are the Windows-inapplicable macOS cases).
- `tsc -p tsconfig.json --noEmit`: clean.
- `pnpm ci:l1` could not run on this host: the tagged runner spawns `pnpm` without a shell and this machine only has a `pnpm.cmd` shim (spawn ENOENT). CI runs the same gate; the local suite and typecheck above are the local evidence.

No behaviour change for a correct tree: the preflight only reads a lockfile and asks the venv for its versions.

1221.body:
Desktop users need Web to manage execution resources and inspect model usage. This brings those capabilities into Desktop's existing settings layout, makes environments clearly belong to a Runner, and adds compact token statistics both in settings and below conversation replies.

Closes #1220.

The release-version CI correction is tracked separately in #1269; this PR's diff contains no release-gate changes.

## Changes

- Combine remote machines and scientific environments into Runtime environments. The overview contains registered Runners and global Conda/Pip sources; Runner details contain connection, resources and environment management. Package sources save quietly, and environment creation uses creation-specific feedback.
- Add execution quotas, JiuwenSwarm paid-search credentials and webpage-fetch selection, and network proxy configuration. DeepSeek search/fetch share a key. Proxy selection, connection testing and bypass editing use compact grouped controls; custom proxy URLs can be viewed and edited.
- Add deployment-wide model usage with date filters, total/input/output tokens and a flat model table. Below each finished conversation turn, add a token badge with an expandable model/token breakdown. Omit unreported fields and avoid counting cache or reasoning tokens twice.
- Record JiuwenSwarm task usage at the model gateway before SDK defaults can turn missing reasoning into zero. Keep platform main/child accounting separate and ignore duplicate SDK reports. Existing usage records are not rewritten.
- Remove project Runner selection from system settings. Unspecified selection follows the registered Runner catalog dynamically; explicit selections and admission restrictions remain enforced. No session Runner picker is introduced.

Analytics reporting fields are additive; exchange rates remain enabled by default for existing clients. Existing Web settings remain available. Dormant DeepSeek credentials require an explicit re-save to enable search rather than being silently activated.

## Validation

Focused checks performed during implementation:

- Runtime-settings browser journeys: **14 mocked-backend Playwright cases passed**, including registration, detail navigation, connection/resources, credentials, deletion, NPU selection, and no project-availability writes. Both real-backend Runner cases were updated and successfully collected (not executed); targeted TypeScript checking of both specifications and their imported helpers passed.

- Resource/settings regressions: **156 passed, 0 failed** (Desktop 116, schema/API 38, focused store 2).
- Conversation and per-turn usage regressions: **150 passed, 0 failed**, including existing transcript/configuration behavior; follow-up usage-label checks: **6 passed**.
- JiuwenSwarm gateway, agent, orchestration and usage-accounting regressions: **240 passed, 0 failed**.
- Latest bypass-layout change: **1 focused save regression passed**. Affected-package type checks, targeted test type checks, and Desktop/API builds passed during implementation; `git diff --check` passed.
- CI regression checks: **8 app-model-setup render scenarios, 6 turn-usage tests, and 16 analytics tests passed**; `tsc -p tsconfig.tests.json` passed. App fixtures include the session usage endpoint, and analytics fixtures supply the required context maps.
- Runner-selection review regressions: **35 Web, 14 schema/API, and 28 Desktop tests passed**. Catalog loading cannot seed a partial override; unspecified availability does not imply an existing remote workspace. Web/API/Desktop and shared test type checks passed.
- Verified in a disposable worktree that all 16 feature commits can be rebased onto upstream main `f10ac0fe` without conflicts. The published branch history is preserved.

The browser capture below verifies rendering and navigation in both interface languages against an existing JiuwenSwarm backend. It does not exercise settings writes or paid model calls. Full local UT/ST/E2E gates and native Electron platform checks were not run; the current Actions run reports CI results.
