1224.author: yuanzhou75
1224.body:
Closes #1169

One PR for the whole journey, as the issue asks: start a research, watch its tree grow, read a node, control it, and come back to it later. The surface follows the desktop's Evolve — a card in the conversation, a task-oriented panel, a readable tree and one node's detail — and the data stays Idea Tree's own: nothing is forced into Evolve's candidate/score model, and a value the backend did not report is shown as unavailable.

This PR delivers the desktop client. The web client is out of scope: #1169's first delivery is the desktop journey and the web is the behaviour reference.

## What the desktop does

**Start: the agent-driven path.** `/idea-tree <task>` and `/idea-tree-team <task>` are ordinary messages. The agent runs the preparation its skill requires — literature and evidence — and calls `create_idea_research`, so `materials` travels and the team prefix keeps its meaning. The client never creates a research: it recognises the command only to know one is expected, re-reads the session's list while the command is in flight (bounded to five minutes), and opens that research's panel when it appears. Reopening a session, or restarting the app, shows the persisted cards and opens nothing by itself.

**Settings.** Settings › 智能 › Idea Tree (`apps/desktop/src/views/settings/IdeaTreeSettings.tsx`) reads and writes `GET/PUT /api/settings/idea-tree` with the field set the API accepts (`templateId`, `explorationIntensity`, `maxTokens`, `maxTokensPerCall`, `maxDepth`, `maxNodes`, `scoreDirection`, the three prompt overrides, per-stage thinking effort). The retired rounds / candidates / assessor-weight fields are neither rendered nor sent. A 503 renders as an actionable prerequisite, not an empty form.

**The card.** `apps/desktop/src/views/idea/IdeaResearchCard.tsx`: an Evolve-style run card whose whole body is the button — tree mark, objective folded to one line, phase · round · batch progress · tokens, and a state chip that turns while the research is live. An unreported token count stays "not reported" (never 0), an unknown phase is printed verbatim, and a completed or ended research offers no start action.

**The panel.** The 任务 tab of the right column, the same place an Evolve run opens. `apps/desktop/src/views/idea/IdeaResearchPanel.tsx` reads the persisted research on open, follows the SSE stream while the engine says it is live, offers only the controls the status allows, and re-reads when a control is refused. **结束 asks first** — it cannot be resumed — and the tree it already grew stays.

**The tree.** `apps/desktop/src/views/idea/IdeaTree.tsx` draws the shape the research grew: one row per depth, siblings side by side, each parent centred over its children, an arrow per branch, a dashed arrow into a pruned node and a live dot on the running one. Direction and candidate differ by shape and tint. Leaves are laid out in reading order and an orphan is still drawn, so nothing the engine reported disappears. The drawing scales to the column down to 0.6 and scrolls past that rather than shrinking text.

**Node detail.** Reads `stages` — design, assessor stages, aggregate — because a node has no `design`/`assessments` field: a missing stage is "unavailable", a null score is not 0 while a reported 0 is a score, and a null `pruneReason` reads as "not pruned".

**Recovery.** A dropped stream is not the end of the panel: it refetches and reconnects with a backoff (1 s doubling to 30 s, four attempts), because every frame is a whole view and a refetch is the current state. A 503 or a list failure is said in the conversation above the cards, so an unreadable list never looks like an empty session, and the notice clears once a later read works. The panel's 503 state offers 重试.

**Legacy.** Sessions written before the research API carry their tree on `GET /api/sessions/:id/idea-tree/graph`. They get the read-only card and panel the issue asks for (`apps/desktop/src/views/idea/LegacyIdeaTree.tsx`): the drawing, a node's detail, and no controls.

**Evolve stays intact.** 任务 shows one thing at a time: opening a run clears any selected research or legacy tree, and opening a research clears the run. Both surfaces work in one session.

## Verification

- `tsc -p apps/desktop --noEmit`: clean.
- `vite build` (apps/desktop): succeeds; only the pre-existing chunk-size warning.
- The whole desktop suite on this machine: **177 tests, 74 pass, 0 fail, 103 skipped**. Every one of the 103 prints the same reason — `host windows/amd64 is not declared by os:linux` — so the split is **103 `os:linux`, 0 `os:darwin`, 0 for a missing dependency or an unbuilt workspace**: the 74 that ran did so in the same process against the same install. Those 103 are the suite's own platform tags; the `apps/desktop` tests are in the tagged runner's `nodeSources`, so the Linux `UT` job is where they execute.
- The Idea Tree suites, run here: **44/44** (`idea-tree-api` 4, `card` 4, `panel` 8, `view` 8, `list` 5, `stale-node` 1, `task-tab` 2, `settings` 3, `legacy` 4, `awaiting` 5).
- `apps/desktop/tests/support/app-model-setup-render.ts`, the harness behind the `os:linux` App render tests, renders **8/8** scenarios × locale here; it now knows the two Idea Tree reads a session makes.
- `pnpm ci:l1`: **not run on this host** — the l1 profile targets `linux/amd64` and the runner reports `planned: 4, executed: 0, passed: 0`, so CI is the word on it.
- The real Electron shell is **not covered here**: `apps/desktop/e2e` (Playwright driving the Electron app) is not wired into any workflow, and the captures below come from `vite dev` with the repository's fixtures. Window chrome and the IPC bridge under the real preload are therefore unverified for this PR — a gap that predates this change.

**CI on the previous head `bdbe85f0`** ran UT → `failure`, and `merge-gate` followed it. The failure is real and is fixed in this head: App now reads a session's researches, and that render harness recorded the read as an unexpected request (4 tests: `new-session` / `new-project` × two locales). The harness now answers both routes and renders 8/8 here. This head's run is the check.

## Screenshots

Desktop shell on `vite dev` with the repository's `e2e/fixtures` control plane plus mocked Idea Tree routes, 1440×900, zh-CN and en. Every capture is taken after a DOM assertion, and each row says what that assertion is.

| the research card | the card carries phase · round · batch · tokens and the live chip (`执行叶子 / 第 2 轮 / 本轮 1/3 / 268290 tokens / 正在优化`) | ![zh card](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/yuanzhou75/sciencediscovery/screenshots-1169/docs/screenshots/1169/rework/v4-zh-CN-card.png) | ![en card](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/yuanzhou75/sciencediscovery/screenshots-1169/docs/screenshots/1169/rework/v4-en-card.png) |

| one node's detail | the pruned candidate's hypothesis, status, search state, score `0.4`, design, aggregate and prune reason | ![zh detail](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/yuanzhou75/sciencediscovery/screenshots-1169/docs/screenshots/1169/rework/v4-zh-CN-detail.png) | ![en detail](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/yuanzhou75/sciencediscovery/screenshots-1169/docs/screenshots/1169/rework/v4-en-detail.png) |
| 结束 asks first | after the first press nothing is ended: the footer reads the warning plus 取消 / 结束 | ![zh end](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/yuanzhou75/sciencediscovery/screenshots-1169/docs/screenshots/1169/rework/v4-zh-CN-end-confirm.png) | ![en end](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/yuanzhou75/sciencediscovery/screenshots-1169/docs/screenshots/1169/rework/v4-en-end-confirm.png) |
| a paused research | status 已暂停 and exactly 继续 / 结束 — no 暂停 | ![zh paused](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/yuanzhou75/sciencediscovery/screenshots-1169/docs/screenshots/1169/rework/v4-zh-CN-paused.png) | ![en paused](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/yuanzhou75/sciencediscovery/screenshots-1169/docs/screenshots/1169/rework/v4-en-paused.png) |

| straight after `/idea-tree` | zero cards before the command, then one card and the panel open by itself (tab is 任务) — nothing was clicked | ![zh after start](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/yuanzhou75/sciencediscovery/screenshots-1169/docs/screenshots/1169/rework/v4-zh-CN-after-start.png) | ![en after start](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/yuanzhou75/sciencediscovery/screenshots-1169/docs/screenshots/1169/rework/v4-en-after-start.png) |
| Settings › 智能 › Idea Tree | the shipped field set (15 inputs: template, intensity, direction, depth, nodes, tokens, per-call tokens, the three prompts, five per-stage efforts) | ![zh settings](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/yuanzhou75/sciencediscovery/screenshots-1169/docs/screenshots/1169/rework/v4-zh-CN-settings.png) | ![en settings](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/yuanzhou75/sciencediscovery/screenshots-1169/docs/screenshots/1169/rework/v4-en-settings.png) |

## The reviews on `bdbe85f0`

| item | where it is now |
| --- | --- |
| the launch dialog replaced the agent path (`materials` lost, `/idea-tree-team` flattened, contract divergence) | **the dialog is deleted.** `/idea-tree[-team]` is a message again; `createIdeaResearch` and the dialog's component and tests are gone. Settings live in Settings › Idea Tree, as `skills/idea-tree-team/SKILL.md` says. |
| `onStarted` dropped the created view, so a start never opened the panel | the client no longer creates anything. It re-reads the list while the command is in flight and opens the research that appears — the "straight after `/idea-tree`" capture above asserts it. |
| 任务 preferred a research over an Evolve run, so Evolve's detail was unreachable | opening either one clears the other (`showEvolveRun` / `showIdeaResearch`), and the legacy tree too. |
| 结束 ended a research on one click | two steps, with the consequence on screen (`结束 asks first` capture). |
| the stream effect was keyed on `status`, so a dropped stream never reconnected | a failed stream refetches and reconnects with a backoff, four attempts; a successful read clears the 503 notice, and the 503 state has 重试. |
| `useIdeaResearches`'s `unavailable`/`error` were never rendered | both are shown above the cards, so a 503 or a failed list is not an empty session. |
| `getIdeaTreeGraph` had no caller (legacy trees had no surface) | wired: read-only card + panel, with its own tests. |
| `ideaTreeCommand` / `ideaTreeCommandTask` unused | deleted; only `isIdeaTreeCommand` stays, for the "a research is expected" signal. |
| the body described a Settings change the diff did not contain | this body describes the settings entry that exists in this head. |
| the "paused" and "just started" captures | both above, in both locales. |
| the auto-open baseline (second round) | the ids a finished read already had are the baseline, so a slow first read is not news and a fast agent still opens its research; `stepAwaitingIdea` pins both directions |
| a session's list belongs to that session (third round) | switching sessions clears `views`/`loads`/`error`/`unavailable` and drops a read for a session that is no longer current; two tests cover a switch while the read is pending, and the same switch when it fails |

1225.author: ink999107
1225.body:
The repository already contains skills, specialists and connectors, but they are only discoverable by reading the tree, and a research session package (`.sdresearch`) has no home at all once it is produced. This adds the hub. A build-time exporter projects the tracked sources into download artifacts and an import catalogue; the database is the source of the site's browse payload (`GET /api/v1/catalog`); nginx serves the site beside the API, so page, catalogue and downloads share one origin. Accounts, uploads, version history, review and short-lived download links live behind `/api/v1`, modelled on the openJiuwen Agentic Hub reference, and the importer carries the existing catalogue across.

Earlier this was two pull requests (#1225 and #1243); they now ship as one change, because the site switch and the importer only make sense with the service.

## The site (`apps/hub`)

Five tabs — skills, team skills, specialists, connectors and session packages — share one category tree, a searchable list and a detail view. Routes are real paths (`/skills/<id>`, `/teams/<id>`, `/sessions/<id>`), so a refresh or a shared link resolves to the same asset. Every asset exposes its README and a download. The UI is bilingual (zh/en) and follows the Agentic Hub reference: gradient hero, per-tab counts, segmented tabs, a pill search, an icon-led rail that becomes a chip strip below 900 px, and the reference's 1600 px container with a 1536 px detail card.

Downloads open the browser's save dialog where the browser has one (Chrome and Edge), so the file goes to the folder the person picks; the bytes come from a same-origin `/api/v1/artifacts/{id}/content` endpoint, which a private bucket needs no CORS rule for, and the plain navigation to the presigned URL remains the fallback. Session headers show a localized run time and the model the package recorded; obvious placeholders such as `local-*` are not shown as if they were a model.

Detail pages carry the tile, name, category, version pill and the primary download; beneath them a reading column (description, Readme and Files tabs) sits beside a "Basic information" card that shows only fields the catalog carries. Files is a two-pane browser: the left pane lists exactly what the archive holds — SKILL.md plus every resource, with its size — and the right pane renders the selected file in place, markdown for `.md`, a source listing for text files, a note instead of a preview for binaries.

## The exporter (`scripts/hub`)

`pnpm hub:export` reads only tracked sources — `skills/`, `packages/specialist/src/builtins.ts`, `packages/mcp-sources/src/*` and `extensions_config.json` — and writes `apps/hub/public/`, which is gitignored because every input is tracked. Skill and specialist archives are built in memory (`fflate`), so an export needs no network and no temporary directory. Each skill's files are also copied to `skills/<id>/<path>` (44 files, 0.42 MB) so the Files tab never unpacks a zip in the browser.

## External skills and session packages

`pnpm hub:sync-skills` freezes a snapshot of the MindScienceSkills tree (364 skills) from GitCode into `snapshot.tar.gz` and `index.json`; extraction refuses absolute paths and `..` entries.

A session drop is `<id>.sdresearch` plus an `<id>.json` sidecar, and publication is all-or-nothing: one bad package aborts before the first byte is written. Verification enforces the contract — 50 MiB cap, whole-file sha256, the manifest inventory, `records.json` hashed but never parsed. The published `sessions/index.json` is the persistent index; a run merges by id, a package leaves only through an explicit `unpublish`, and unpublishing leaves the uploaded file in place so old links keep working.

## Deployment

The site is served by nginx at `/`, which proxies `/api/` to the service, so page, catalogue and download content share one origin. `docker-compose.yml` runs MySQL, the API and nginx on one host; `pnpm hub:build:api --root` builds the site without the exporter, and the database is the source of the browse payload (`GET /api/v1/catalog`).

The static publishing workflows are gone: a production write is a deployment, not a push to `main`. The exporter remains as the importer's input, and `pnpm hub:sync-skills` remains a manual snapshot step.

## The backend (`services/hub-api`)

FastAPI + SQLAlchemy. The reference establishes the shape: an asset row carrying what the site shows, a version row carrying what a download serves, review state on the version, and `public_latest_version` deciding what is listed. This keeps that contract and differs where our data does: five asset kinds in one lifecycle (`skill`, `team`, `specialist`, `connector`, `session`) instead of six per-type models; no plugin-specific schema validation; stateless HMAC session tokens instead of Redis, so the database is the only stateful dependency; and the reference's `{code, message, data}` envelope and `/api/v1/...` paths.

Uploads are validated before anything is written: the 50 MiB cap measured on the bytes rather than `Content-Length`, path traversal, absolute paths, backslashes, encrypted and duplicate entries, an uncompressed-size ceiling, and a per-entry sha256 inventory that becomes the Files tab. Downloads resolve through `GET /api/v1/artifacts/{id}`, which checks visibility and returns a short-lived presigned URL. Registration closes after the first account, which is the administrator; later accounts come from the administrator.

## Storage and data placement

One private bucket; keys are `assets/<kind>/<publisher>/<asset>/<version>/<filename>` composed in one function. Nothing is anonymously readable, and a bucket listing is refused. Metadata — assets, versions, manifests, users, review state, audit — lives in the database; the bytes live in the bucket; the site and its `catalog.json` remain static files served by the front end.

## Importer and site switch

`scripts/import_catalog.py` reads the exporter's `catalog.json` and writes the same data into the database and the bucket: it preserves catalogue ids, verifies each artifact against the catalogue's sha256 before uploading, wraps single-file specialists and connectors in a one-entry archive while checking the digest against the file rather than the wrapper, marks imported versions approved, and is idempotent. `--dry-run` validates without writing.

The site gets one build-time switch: with `VITE_HUB_API_BASE=/api/v1` the download button asks the API for a URL before navigating, which a private bucket requires; if that call fails the anchor still points at the catalogue URL, so a static deployment is unchanged.

## CI

`hub-api.yml` runs the service's tests and builds its image on changes under `services/hub-api`; it is informational and not part of `merge-gate`. The hub's exporter and site checks run in the UT layer, which builds the workspace: L1 stays the static slice (install only), matching the repository's layering.

## Screenshots

Taken from the built site against the local stack (Chromium, 1440 and 390 CSS px):

| Home, 1440 | Detail with the Files tab, 1440 |
|---|---|
| ![Home at 1440](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/ink999107/sciencediscovery/feat/asset-hub/docs/hub/screenshots/home-1440.png) | ![Detail Files tab](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/ink999107/sciencediscovery/feat/asset-hub/docs/hub/screenshots/detail-files-1440.png) |

| Detail in Chinese, 1440 | Home at 390 |
|---|---|
| ![Chinese detail](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/ink999107/sciencediscovery/feat/asset-hub/docs/hub/screenshots/detail-zh-1440.png) | ![Home at 390](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/ink999107/sciencediscovery/feat/asset-hub/docs/hub/screenshots/home-390.png) |

## Validation

- `pnpm hub:test`: 44 passed (4 suites), including the case asserting every served skill file matches the repository byte for byte.
- `python -m pytest` in `services/hub-api`: 18 passed — registration and its closing, login, tampered tokens, administrator-created accounts, upload → pending → hidden, approval → listed and downloadable with matching sha256, rejection, owner-only uploads, the Files listing and text preview, path-shaped ids through the `%2F` encoding, the size/traversal/non-zip refusals, and the importer end to end including idempotence and a checksum mismatch.
- Importer against the real catalogue: 387 assets, 385 versions, two session packages skipped because their `.sdresearch` files were not in the site tree.
- `pnpm --filter @sciencediscovery/hub typecheck`, `pnpm build`, and the hub build with and without the API switch.
- The earlier static-hub layers (UT 7718 planned / 7687 executed / 7670 passed, ST 63 planned / 62 passed, mocked E2E 188 planned / 181 passed) were measured on `de624faa`; the failures are this host's known constants and are itemised in the commit history of the branch. UI-only commits after that re-ran typecheck, build and `hub:test`.

## E2E user journeys

**Static site — PASS.** Driven in headless Chromium at 1440, 768 and 390 CSS px in English and 390 in Chinese: `document.scrollWidth` equals `clientWidth` on home and detail pages, the rail becomes a chip strip below 900 px, deep links resolve after a reload, session READMEs are fetched from the sibling prefix, and the Files browser lists and previews the archive's contents. A publication increment kept the entries it did not deliver (1 → 2 → 3 packages, every earlier URL still 200), and unpublishing removed only the named id while its file still returned 200.

**Backend — PASS on a local stack.** MySQL 8.0 (container) + the service + the built site + the real bucket, driven over HTTP and in Chromium; not yet on a deployment host.

- Import into MySQL and OBS: 387 assets, 385 versions; two sessions skipped as above.
- `http://127.0.0.1:8612/site/skills/antibody-design`: the button's static `href` is `/site/packages/antibody-design-1.0.0.zip`; the click issues `GET /api/v1/artifacts/antibody-design?version=1.0.0` and the presigned URL serves 109171 bytes whose sha256 equals the catalogue's.
- The path-id external skill `astronomy/astronomical_analysis/astropy`: the click issues `GET /api/v1/artifacts/astronomy%2Fastronomical_analysis%2Fastropy?version=snapshot-20261117` and the download's sha256 equals the catalogue's.
- Over HTTP, not the test client: administrator login, create, upload (`201`, `pending`), approve, download; the bytes match, and the test asset and object were removed.
- The bucket is private: an unsigned `GET` of an object returns `403`, as does a bucket listing.
- The save dialog path was driven in Chromium with the picker stubbed (headless cannot show the dialog): suggested name `antibody-design-1.0.0.zip`, 109171 bytes written, equal to the catalogue's size; the session header reads `Run at Nov 17, 2026, 6:38 AM` and `Model DeepSeek-V4.1-Flash-1017`, with no `local-smoke`.

Building against the real bucket surfaced three fixes now in the branch: boto3 1.36+ adds a CRC32 trailer OBS rejects (`XAmzContentSHA256Mismatch`); external skill ids are paths up to 88 characters (84 exceed 64), so columns are 191 and routes use a path converter; and the development host's clock is 28 minutes fast, which SigV4 rejects — the smoke tooling compensates, the service deliberately does not, and its README states that the deployment host must run NTP.

## Release

Release category: `release:feature` — the GitHub label is pending a maintainer, because this account has no write access to the upstream repository's labels.

User impact: a static site lists the repository's skills, specialists, connectors and session packages with READMEs and downloads; assets can also be published into a service with accounts, review and version history, served from a private bucket through short-lived links.

Compatibility and migration: none for existing behaviour. New app, new service, new scripts and three workflows. The database schema is created at startup and the importer is the migration path from `catalog.json`; the static publishing pipeline keeps working while the backend is introduced.

1226.body:
Desktop Settings can manage existing Specialists, but users need the legacy Web UI to create a custom one. This change adds **Add specialist** to the Desktop Specialists page, including when the list is empty.

The action opens the shared form with a blank Native/Full-access draft. Name, description, and instructions are required. The form uses the API's description/instructions limits of 500/20,000 characters. A successful save refreshes the list. A refused save keeps the draft for retry. Reopening the session Specialist picker refreshes the catalog and preserves the current selection.

Closes #1180.

## Specialist role composition

Selecting a Specialist uses `BASE_WORKSPACE_SYSTEM_PROMPT` for platform tool, permission, workspace, artifact and evidence rules, followed by the selected Specialist's description and instructions. Ordinary sessions also receive the default science-analysis role and general workflow from `WORKSPACE_SYSTEM_PROMPT`. The shared composer supplies both the native Agent and the SD prompt sent to the JiuwenSwarm adapter. JiuwenSwarm's own framework prompt is governed by its configured prompt mode. Prompt manifests use version `m8.5.0`.

**Product decision confirmed by the requester on 2026-11-21 and recorded in #1180.** Each Specialist defines its role and workflow. The generic SD identity and general data-analysis workflow are replaced when a Specialist is selected. The platform execution and governance rules remain in the base. The English and Chinese form hints and guides describe this composition.

## Validation on the reviewed head

Commit `e9ba1dc7ce90088b523281160a662b61dba9ba6f`, rebased onto `348b4db468fbdf4bbca36542fd01919f8c89cde0`.

- WSL workspace build and workspace/API/Desktop typechecks passed.
- Workspace package tests: **143 passed, 0 failed**.
- Native Agent and JiuwenSwarm adapter integration tests: **168 passed, 0 failed**. Added cases inspect the actual model/adapter requests for Specialist instructions, removal of the default SD role and retention of permission/artifact rules.
- Focused desktop settings/composer unit tests: **75 passed, 0 failed**.
- Desktop Specialist browser journeys on Windows Chrome: **6 passed, 0 failed, 0 skipped, 0 flaky**, in **34.4 seconds** on 2026-11-21.
- [CI run 44916136088](https://github.com/openJiuwen-ai/sciencediscovery/actions/runs/44916136088) succeeded on this head. L1, UT, ST, Coverage, Docker image, both Runner binary builds and merge-gate passed. GitCode CodeCheck also passed.
- The PR profile skips mocked browser E2E, real E2E and desktop installer jobs. The six Desktop journeys above are the local browser validation.
- The browser journeys use a stateful mocked API. A full Desktop-to-real-backend persistence journey remains a validation gap.

Prompt regression cases:
- [Default, Specialist and subagent prompt tests](https://github.com/wyhohyw/sciencediscovery/blob/e9ba1dc7ce90088b523281160a662b61dba9ba6f/packages/workspace/src/prompt.test.ts#L152).

The first-create case verifies the saved card and exactly one create request.

The latest run on 2026-11-21 completed with **6 passed, 0 failed, 0 skipped, 0 flaky**, in **34.4 seconds**. These are browser journeys for `apps/desktop` using a stateful mocked API. ## Release

Release category: `release:feature`

1227.body:
Desktop MCP import now offers **Paste JSON / Upload JSON file**. Choosing a UTF-8 JSON file fills the existing editable import dialog and previews its servers automatically; users review it and confirm **Import servers** before any configuration is saved.

Refs #1178. This extends the issue's scope with the requested file-import flow and retains the remaining default/STDIO-argument fixes. Main's existing creation, OAuth controls, tool previews and discovery flow are preserved.

## Changes

- Keep one Add server / Import toolbar. The Import dropdown supports pointer and keyboard navigation, outside dismissal and Escape without closing Settings.
- Reuse `mcpServers` parsing and the existing per-server import endpoint. Preserve arguments, environment variables, headers and transport settings; imported servers remain disabled. Successful entries are retained when another server is rejected, with each outcome displayed.
- Auto-fill a full-width JSON editor and preview after native file selection. Accept a UTF-8 BOM; reject files over 1.5 MB and configurations over 50 entries. Invalid, empty or unreadable files show localized errors without importing. Cancel the picker without changes; edit the JSON or select the same filename again to recover.
- Disable repeated import, editing and modal dismissal while requests are pending. Pass `closeDisabled={busy}` to both import and manual modals, also addressing optional review F4.
- Retain the disabled / Streamable HTTP / 60-second creation defaults, integer timeout validation from 1–600 seconds, per-line STDIO arguments and preservation of untouched legacy argument arrays. Pending OAuth authorization cannot produce a successful test toast.
- Update the English/Chinese configuration guide and MCP protocol section 5.2 to match the desktop flow. No backend or API change.

## Test coverage

- Desktop unit regressions cover defaults, cancellation/reset, form validation, legacy arguments, OAuth feedback, file auto-fill, invalid/unreadable/oversized files, and pending-request guards.
- `apps/desktop/e2e/mcp-import.spec.ts` covers keyboard navigation, the existing paste/cancel flow, BOM file auto-fill and preview, individual import outcomes, malformed JSON and same-filename recovery.
- `apps/desktop/e2e/settings-interactions.spec.ts` covers manual creation, editing, retry, default-source selection, connection feedback, secret validation and deletion.

The API / Runner / SDK Echo journey in `apps/desktop/e2e-stack/custom-mcp.spec.ts` covers:

1. Open and cancel manual creation; verify disabled / HTTP / 60-second defaults.
2. Upload an Echo JSON file, preview without saving, confirm import and inspect the disabled saved configuration and spaced arguments.
3. Test the saved connection and discover tools while it remains disabled.
4. Enable the server and independently select the default source.
5. Edit its description, reload and verify persistence.
6. Call Echo from a conversation and verify the tool result, invocation record and reloaded answer.
7. Cancel deletion, then confirm it; reload and verify removal of the server and its default-source reference.

Desktop unit regressions are included in the existing CI UT catalog. Browser journey setup is documented in `apps/desktop/e2e/README.md` and `apps/desktop/e2e-stack/README.md`.

See [GitHub Actions checks](https://github.com/openJiuwen-ai/sciencediscovery/pull/1227/checks) for gate results and logs.

1228.author: wyhohyw
1228.body:
Saved artifacts can disappear from a Desktop conversation when a terminal run's event history is pruned or unavailable. This increment recovers those cards and lets readers expand additional files in place.

Refs #1202.

## Increment on #1257

#1257 already delivered the card presentation, per-run grouping, subagent lineage walk, kind ordering and exact-version panel preview. This branch retains those implementations. The superseded full-width list and shared-schema selector from the old #1228 head are removed from the PR diff.

- Retain terminal SessionRun rows independently of replay, using the existing Session/epoch guards and bounded cache.
- Attach one strip to a replayed answer, a stored answer, or the run's status after its starting message when no answer survives. Do not synthesize empty turns without eligible outputs.
- Recover missing subagent lineage from the existing catalog; cache successful reads and retry failures on the next outputs refresh, including another version from the same child. Ignore stale Session/client reads.
- Keep main's five-card selection; expand remaining files, including intermediate kinds, within the same strip, with collapse and a panel action.
- Keep known queued/running/blocked outputs hidden even after the event connection closes. Preserve terminal failure/cancellation and usage presentation.

- Keep keyboard focus inside the disclosure after Enter on either toggle; both controls identify the same list with `aria-controls` and expose `aria-expanded`. The browser regression asserts focus and the list association in both directions.

No new endpoint, schema change or second grouping/rendering implementation. Design: [English](https://github.com/openJiuwen-ai/sciencediscovery/blob/1a717200a99a9fe7bb530995e2eabeb31330aa15/docs/en/design/desktop-artifact-recovery.md) / [中文](https://github.com/openJiuwen-ai/sciencediscovery/blob/1a717200a99a9fe7bb530995e2eabeb31330aa15/docs/zh/design/desktop-artifact-recovery.md) (files included in this PR). The closing keyword is deliberately **Refs**, crediting #1257 for the acceptance it already delivered rather than claiming the entire original feature here.

## Verification

Functional validation and capture source: `1a717200a99a9fe7bb530995e2eabeb31330aa15`. Current head `e2c4015c1831c2fe2bab76e432a443ba82f21deb` adds only the 12 PNG files; executable application code is identical to that tested source. The implementation remains linear on main `a8573558f8c372854079a65906171b3a543b6fb7`, with no merge commit. Old head `12dedcb94` is preserved in a local backup branch.

| Check | Actual result |
| --- | --- |
| Desktop typecheck | Passed |
| Complete Desktop unit suite | **1405 passed, 0 failed, 0 skipped**; test concurrency limited to 2 after an initial unrelated App-render subprocess timeout under parallel repository load |
| Desktop conversation, artifact recovery and panel browser journeys | **18 passed, 0 failed, 0 skipped** |
| zh-CN / English screenshot journeys | **2 passed**, producing the 12 images below |
| Architecture boundaries / design Markdown | Passed on the integrated implementation |
| Repository build | Passed; including the final-head build used by repository E2E |

The browser journeys render the actual Desktop app in the isolated WSL Vite harness (private port 14275), with page-owned API fixtures and no live LLM calls. 1230.author: zhaochen39
1230.body:
Nightly research-1 failed on DRB-58 after the model returned HTTP 200 and reset every streaming attempt. This PR makes the gateway recovery path actionable and extends the bounded stream retry budget so transient interruptions do not fail the turn after only two retries.

## Changes

- Convert invalid or stale sandbox network authorization failures into retryable tool guidance that asks for a fresh authorization and a new execution.
- Increase interrupted streaming retries from 2 to 4, for at most 5 total upstream requests, and update the regression coverage for the new bound.
- Align the workspace prompt regression and sandbox tool tests with the new authorization guidance and the `unknown` details contract.

## Validation

- Targeted JiuwenSwarm model gateway test: 67 passed, 0 failed.
- Targeted workspace prompt and sandbox network tests: 25 passed, 0 failed.
- Recursive package typecheck and `tsconfig.tests.json` typecheck: passed.
- GitHub Actions L1 slice on the PR head: 4 planned, 4 executed, 4 passed.
- Full UT/ST/mocked-E2E slices were not run locally during PR preparation at the request of the operator. The nightly UT failure that motivated the follow-up was reproduced from its uploaded evidence and fixed here.

## E2E user journeys

BLOCKED for local PR preparation. The affected user journey is the real DRB-58 research run documented in issue #1222; it requires the configured live model service and was not invoked locally. Expected outcome: the research turn completes and declares its final artifacts after transient stream interruptions. The existing nightly run reached the provider-fault path instead.

## Release

Release category: release:fix
User impact: Research runs tolerate up to four interrupted stream retries and receive actionable recovery guidance for stale sandbox network authorization.
Compatibility and migration: None.

Fixes #1222

1231.author: yuanzhou75
1231.body:
Closes #1229

`#1229` reports that the Idea Tree research list fails on a Chinese Windows host with `UnicodeDecodeError: 'gbk' codec can't decode byte 0x80`, while `get` for the same running research succeeds. The root cause is a codec asymmetry, not a listing bug.

## What is actually broken

- The write path is UTF-8 on both stores: `research.py:106` opens the temporary with `encoding='utf-8'` and `:109` dumps with `ensure_ascii=False`; `idea_tree_service.py:31` does the same.
- Three read paths left the codec to the host: `ResearchStore.read` (`research.py:129`), `ResearchStore.list` (`research.py:133`), and `IdeaTreeStore.call` (`idea_tree_service.py:49`).
- `get` only looked healthy because `research_service.py:88-95` answers a research that is in `_running` from memory, so it never decoded anything; `list` (`:148-149`) always goes through the store. A research that is paused, completed, or predates a restart takes the same decode on `get` — that is a read failure, not a missing row.

## What changed

- `ResearchStore.read` and `ResearchStore.list` read with `encoding='utf-8'`.
- `IdeaTreeStore.call` reads `state.json` with `encoding="utf-8"`.
- No behaviour, format, or key change: the bytes on disk are already UTF-8, so this only stops the reader from guessing.

## Tests

Two cases, both on the mechanism that actually fails:

- `test_a_research_with_non_ascii_content_reads_on_a_non_utf8_host` — writes a research whose title is CJK through `ResearchStore.save`, then reads it through both `read()` and `list()` **in a child interpreter whose default text encoding is ASCII** (`PYTHONUTF8=0 LC_ALL=C`). That is the same decode path cp936 takes, so the case fails on the bug and passes on the fix instead of passing vacuously on a UTF-8 runner.
- `test_a_tree_with_non_ascii_content_reads_on_a_non_utf8_host` — the same probe against `IdeaTreeStore.call` (`readTree`) after a create with a CJK objective.

Both child processes also assert that an un-encoded `read_text()` on the same file raises `UnicodeDecodeError`, so a probe that stops being able to see the bug fails loudly instead of passing quietly. (That sentence was in the first revision of this body before the assertion existed in the file — it is true as of `837fb62e27c0`, which is what review round 1 asked for.)

Both cases are mutation-checked: with the fix each child exits 0, and with the encoding removed again each exits 1 on `UnicodeDecodeError`.

## Verification — run for real, on a Chinese Windows host

Both halves of the suite were executed against `a6a06c99bc5c` in a real environment: Windows, where the default text codec is **cp936**, with real `fastapi 0.163.2`, `pydantic 2.14.3`, `pytest 9.2.0` and `httpx 0.28.1` installed into a throwaway venv. No stand-ins.

```
both suites             -> 37 passed, 2 warnings
the two new cases       -> 2 passed, 35 deselected
```

Then the mutation check — the fix is removed again and the same two cases must go red:

```
encoding removed again  -> 2 failed, 35 deselected
   tests/test_idea_research.py::test_a_research_with_non_ascii_content_reads_on_a_non_utf8_host
   tests/test_idea_tree.py::test_a_tree_with_non_ascii_content_reads_on_a_non_utf8_host
   UnicodeDecodeError: 'gbk' codec can't decode byte 0xbd in position 90
   UnicodeDecodeError: 'gbk' codec can't decode byte 0xac in position 116
restored                -> 2 passed, 35 deselected
```

Two things this establishes that a stand-in run could not:

- The failure on the buggy code is `'gbk' codec can't decode ...` — the exact mechanism #1229 reports, reproduced by the test rather than described by it. On a cp936 host the probe does not even need the forced-ASCII child; the environment is already the reported one.
- Running for real found a defect in my own test: `create(api, key='non-ascii', objective=...)` raised `TypeError: dict() got multiple values for keyword argument 'objective'`, because the helper passed the literal keyword and `**overrides` together. The earlier stand-in run reported in review never called this helper, so it missed the bug. `a6a06c99bc5c` merges the overrides with `payload.update(overrides)`.

Nothing outside `services/evolve/tests/` is touched by this commit.

## Scope completeness — this is the only gap in the service

Every `read_text` in `services/evolve/src` was swept, not just the three sites the report names:

| location | encoding before this PR |
| --- | --- |
| `candidates.py:84` | `"utf-8"` already |
| `measurement.py:178`, `:229` | `"utf-8"` already |
| `probe.py:300` | `"utf-8"` already |
| `script_domain.py:302` | `"utf-8"` already |
| `test_gate_domain.py:187` | `"utf-8"` already |
| `vendor/idea_tree/research.py:129`, `:133` | **missing — fixed here** |
| `vendor/idea_tree/idea_tree_service.py:49` | **missing — fixed here** |

Nine `read_text` calls in total: six already named the encoding, and the three this PR changes were the only ones that did not. `grep -rn "read_text(" services/evolve/src | grep -v encoding` is empty on this head, so there is no remaining site of this kind in the service.


## CI coverage of these cases — measured, and not what I assumed

The two cases live in `services/evolve/tests/`, which is the directory the tagged runner is supposed to collect (`test/support/tagged/profiles.mjs:112-113`: `pythonProjects` contains `evolve`, and `pythonSources(project)` is `services/${project}/tests/test_*.py`). Both files carry `pytestmark = pytest.mark.science_tags(category='ut', os='linux', arch=('amd64', 'arm64'))`, so they are `category:ut` and belong to the UT slice.

On this head the UT job (`134700142074`, run `44274693462`) **succeeded**, and it did prepare the environment — the log shows `Prepare: uv sync --project services/evolve --locked --extra test --extra candidates` at 09:20:34Z. But the executed plan contains no Python at all:

- 681 `Run N/683` entries: `.ts` 474, `.tsx` 159, `.mjs` 43, no extension 5 — **`.py` 0**.
- `services/evolve/tests` appears **0 times** in the job log; `.py::` appears **0 times**.

So these two cases are **not currently exercised by CI**, and the green UT check above must not be read as evidence that they pass. `pnpm evolve:test` exists in `package.json:42` and nothing in `.github/workflows/*.yml` invokes it.

That is a pre-existing gap in how the tagged runner collects Python projects, not something this PR introduces — but it does mean this PR ships with local evidence only:

- `ResearchStore`: `save()` → child interpreter forced to ASCII → `read()` and `list()` return the CJK title; an un-encoded `read_text()` in the same child still raises `UnicodeDecodeError`, which is what proves the probe is not vacuous.
- `IdeaTreeStore`: the same probe, **not run** — it needs `fastapi`/`pydantic` and resolving the evolve environment from this machine could not reach the package index.
- All four edited files byte-compile.

**Question for review:** do you want `pnpm evolve:test` run once by hand against this head before approval, or should the Python collection gap be tracked separately? I did not want to claim CI validation that did not happen.

Closes #1024

The export and import surfaces rebuilt to the mock, plus the page the mock points at. Client-side only: no API, schema, shell or packaging change.

## What changed

**Export dialog.** Two type cards carrying their own badges, one size line under them labelled `未压缩估算` / `Uncompressed estimate` above the cap line, the workspace files as a three-column grid with `全选` / `Select all` and middle-ellipsis names, and the `取消` / `开始导出` pair. The scope explanation is an information marker beside `选择导出类型`.

**Sizes are formatted by magnitude.** `formatBytes` prints B / KB / MB / GB with one decimal from KB up and takes its unit from the number that will be printed, so no level prints its own base. The dialog, the cap and the saved rows share it (`app/format-bytes.ts` → `app/size-units.ts`); a ~910 MiB session used to read `933095.4 KiB`.

**Import.** `导入会话` is its own button under `新建会话`; the dialog is destination picker → one drop-or-choose area → the chosen package as a card with `重新选择` and one meta line (`source title · content objects · record data`).

**Read-only snapshot.** An imported Session says so in the header (`🔒 只读`) and under the transcript, with `继续聊天` to create the independent copy.

**Notices.** They stack in the top-right corner, one per state, each with its own icon, an optional `打开文件位置` and a dismiss button; success retires after 5 s, error after 8 s, and the timers are cleared when a toast is dismissed or the view unmounts. A cancel the user asked for is neutral and never renders the spinner.

**Entry point.** `导出会话` sits in the session row's menu (rename / export / delete); the header carries no export action. The guard is shared (`canExportSession`), so a session whose project is gone says so instead of opening an export that must fail.

**Waiting and failures.** The preview keeps a bounded six-attempt wait with a fresh budget on every open; when it stalls, the sentence only offers what works (recalculate, or cancel and retry later); the poll's own localized terminal sentences reach the alert line and only unrecognized server text is folded into 技术细节.

**设置 › 导出记录 follows the session-management page.** One title, the scope control on the left and search on the right, and the rows in a single bordered container with hairline dividers, a file glyph and quiet icon actions.

## What the design change removed

- **The trajectory switch.** A complete export offers `包含完整科学记忆` only. The `trajectory` state, its call sites, its effect dependency and its string are gone, and `startExport` sends `includeFullTrajectory: false` explicitly.
- **The import preview's omission list.** The preview is one meta line. `continueUnavailable` no longer tells the recipient to "check the import omissions", and `researchPackage.omissions` is deleted.

## Screenshots

Desktop renderer at `cbbc9fd3` (the code is unchanged in `5d6a7560` apart from removing the image folder), mock control plane, 1440×940, one browser per locale. The images are served from `91583c6c`, the commit that carries this set; the folder itself was removed from the branch tip afterwards, so the links name that commit rather than the branch. What the shell would provide is stubbed in the shape the packaged app installs: `sdShell.exportFile` (save dialog → token, `write` → ok) and `sdShell.exportHistory` (three rows, one of them a file that is gone). The mock API answers `/research-package/preview`, `/inspect`, `/import` and `/exports`, plus the Session details for the imported snapshot. Every capture is taken after a DOM assertion, and each section states what that assertion is; nothing is composed by hand.

**1. 导出入口 — the session row's menu.** The header carries no export control any more; the row menu is the entry, next to 重命名 and 删除.

1236.author: Huyvux12
1236.body:
Fixes #1232

A transient HTTP 429 from the model endpoint interrupted an Idea Tree research task immediately: `transport()` only retried `>= 500`, so the research engine recorded the task as `interrupted` instead of waiting and retrying.

## What changed

- `services/evolve/src/sciencediscovery_evolve/vendor/idea_tree/research.py` — `transport()` now retries HTTP 429 within the existing two-attempt budget (one retry), with bounded backoff:
  - Honors a numeric `Retry-After` delay when present (capped at 60 s); otherwise a short fixed backoff (500 ms, mirroring the Agent client).
  - The wait is sliced at 0.25 s and polls `stop_action`, so pause/cancel interrupts the backoff instead of waiting it out.
  - A 429 reporting exhausted quota (`insufficient_quota`) is not retried.
  - Repeated 429s raise `Model HTTP 429: retry budget exhausted after 2 attempts: ...`.
  - Each failed attempt is now read (bounded, as before) and closed; the old 5xx branch neither read nor closed on retry.
  - The retry budget is unchanged at two attempts: the protocol-compatibility suite pins exactly two upstream calls on a persistent provider failure, and enlarging it would need that suite updated in the same change.
- `packages/model/src/client.ts` — `ModelRequestError` now carries the provider's `retry-after` delay (`retryAfterMs`) instead of dropping it.
- `packages/model/src/completion.ts` — the streamed error response forwards `retry-after` to the sidecar; the unary error path does the same when the upstream response carries the header (the undici-built response carries no upstream headers today, so nothing is forwarded on that sub-path).
- `services/api/src/http/response.ts`, `services/api/src/evolution/llm-proxy.ts` — `sendJson` accepts extra headers; the proxy forwards upstream `retry-after` to the sidecar on the error path.
- `docs/en/developer-docs/idea-tree.md`, `docs/zh/developer-docs/idea-tree.md` — the new 429 behavior is documented.

## Repro (before the fix, base `d57fc269`)

With a monkeypatched `urllib.request.urlopen` returning HTTP 429 once (`Retry-After: 1`) and then success:

- `test_transport_retries_transient_429_then_succeeds`: `RuntimeError: Model HTTP 429: {"error": {"type": "rate_limit_exceeded", ...}}` after one attempt.
- `test_run_continues_same_stage_after_transient_429`: research status `interrupted`, not `completed`.

## After the fix

- `services/evolve/tests/test_idea_research.py`: **35 passed** (29 baseline + 6 new).
  - New: transient 429 then success continues the same stage (run completes; first-round ideation attempted twice, later rounds once); repeated 429s stop after 2 attempts with `retry budget exhausted`; permanent-quota 429 is not retried (1 attempt, no wait); pause during a backoff wait raises `Interrupted` (1 attempt, no retry); 5xx retry unchanged (503 then success, 0.5 s backoff).
  - The pinned test at `test_idea_research.py:111-118` was updated deliberately, not weakened: its injected error now reads `Model HTTP 429: retry budget exhausted after 2 attempts`, i.e. what `transport()` raises once its budget is exhausted. The asserted behavior (interrupted run, completed stages reused on resume) is unchanged.
- Full `services/evolve/tests/`: 396 passed, 27 failed. All 27 fail identically on the unmodified base (verified with `git stash`): sandbox-dependent tests (`test_puct_sandbox`, `test_script_domain`, `test_test_gate`, `test_measurement`, `test_puct_end_to_end`) that need a working `bwrap` sandbox, which this machine does not provide. None touch the changed code.
- `packages/model` full suite: **157 passed, 0 failed** (includes new tests: a 429 carries `retryAfterMs: 2000` on the thrown error; a streamed 429 forwards `retry-after: 2`).
- `services/api/src/evolution/llm-proxy.test.ts`: **19 passed, 0 failed** (includes new test: a provider 429 forwards `retry-after: 2` to the sidecar).
- `services/api/src/protocol-compatibility.test.ts`: **12 passed, 0 failed** (includes `transient-provider-error`: 503 then 200, exactly 2 upstream calls; `server-exhausted`: exactly 2 calls).
- `services/api/src/evolution/*.test.ts` + `src/configuration/*.test.ts`: **645 tests, 644 passed, 1 failed** — `evolve-thinking-entry.test.ts` ("public evolution journey preserves low thinking effort through the provider", `Error: Timed out waiting for product outcome` at the run-lookup `until` in `submit()`). Pre-existing environmental failure, not caused by this change: the same test fails identically on unmodified base `d57fc26` (verified in a clean worktree: exit 1, 45.3 s, same timeout error). The journey requires working bubblewrap (stated in its header) and `bwrap` is not installed on this machine, so the search it drives can never settle here.

## Not run

- `pnpm ci:l1`, `pnpm ci:st`, `pnpm ci:e2e`: not run locally. `pnpm ci:ut` needs a working sandbox (`bwrap`); this machine has none, so the UT slice was run as the targeted suites above instead of through the shared runner. CI runs all four slices on the PR.
- E2E: not applicable as a live journey — no user-observable product path changes beyond the retry behavior covered by the tests above; the research still completes, pauses, or interrupts with the same statuses as before.

## Risks checked

- Retry budget is unchanged, so no extra billed attempts beyond the current two; token admission is still decided once in `_ask` before the call, with no re-reservation on retry.
- `Retry-After` is honored for 5xx as well as 429, matching the Agent client (`client.ts` already parses it for both); non-numeric values (e.g. HTTP dates) fall back to the fixed backoff.
- A pause issued while waiting is noticed within 0.25 s; the research then pauses with completed stages preserved (covered by the new run-level test and the existing pause test).
- The `sendJson` change is backward compatible (optional extra headers; all existing callers pass three arguments).

## Release label

This change is a `release:fix` (wrong behaviour in something that already existed). I do not have permission to apply labels on this repository, so please apply `release:fix` when reviewing.

1236.title: fix(idea-tree): retry transient model 429s instead of interrupting research

1240.author: Huyvux12
1240.body:
Refs #1239 (evidence part — see scope below).

## Summary

Nightly run 44361037291, shard `research-11`: the managed Python base setup reached terminal `failed` and J5 was BLOCKED with no executed case. The failure transcript existed in the API response (`setup.error` / `components.conda.error`) but J5 and J3 built their BLOCKED reason from `setup.state` + `setup.message` only, so the transcript never reached the journey report and the next occurrence could not be attributed to an external channel/network problem or to a repository defect.

This PR carries that transcript into the BLOCKED reason. It does **not** investigate the Nightly setup failure itself — that failure is still unconfirmed as a repository defect (same commit, same run, J3 passed the readiness assertion in the L2 job), and it cannot be fixed until a transcript is captured.

## What changed

- `test/helpers/environment-setup.ts`: widened `EnvironmentSetup` with optional `error` and `components` (matching `packages/schema/src/environment.ts:451-485`), and added one shared formatter `formatEnvironmentSetupBlockedReason(setup)`. It returns the existing `state: message` text, appends a length-bounded `setup.error`, and appends `conda: <components.conda.error>` only when it differs from `setup.error`. The bound is 1200 chars, the same as the `#1108` precedent (`MANAGED_SHELL_REASON_LIMIT`).
- `test/journey-real-request.spec.ts` (J5) and `test/journey-prepare-environment.spec.ts` (J3): the BLOCKED reason now goes through the formatter.
- `test/helpers/journeys.ts`: `environmentSetup()` return type widened to the exported `EnvironmentSetup` (no runtime change).
- `test/helpers/environment-setup.unit.ts`: 6 new cases (see below).

A failed setup remains BLOCKED; no pass/fail semantics change. Test helpers/specs only — no runner, API, or workflow change.

## Proof package

1. **Base SHA:** upstream `main` @ `59d05aa70a26801e2e907ca49060329028514608` (merge commit of #1236). Reproduced and fixed on this commit.
2. **Reproduction before the fix:** an out-of-tree probe feeds a failed setup (with `error` and `components.conda.error`) through `waitForEnvironmentSetup` and builds J5's reason exactly as the spec did. The object carries both error fields, but the reason is only `BLOCKED: managed Python base is not ready (failed: Conda environment setup failed)` — the transcript is absent (`LibMambaUnsatisfiableError: false`, `ECONNRESET: false`).
3. **After the fix:** the same probe through the formatter prints the transcript in the reason (`LibMambaUnsatisfiableError: true`, `ECONNRESET: true`), and an identical conda error is printed once. New unit tests fail on base (the formatter does not exist there) and pass after: `node --test test/helpers/environment-setup.unit.ts` → **17/17 pass** (11 pre-existing + 6 new).
4. **Control case:** a setup without `error` renders byte-identically to before — covered for `error` absent, `null`, `""`, whitespace-only, `components: {}`, and `components: { conda: {} }`. The skip condition (`setup.state !== "ready"`) and J3's `.toBe("ready")` assertion are untouched.
5. **Regression scope:**
   - `node --test test/helpers/*.unit.ts`: 53 tests, 50 pass, 3 fail. The 3 failures are file-level load errors (`ERR_MODULE_NOT_FOUND: test/e2e-auth.js`, generated by the E2E global setup and absent from this checkout). Verified pre-existing via `git stash`: same 3 files fail on the clean base (47 tests, 44 pass). No new failure from this diff.
   - `pnpm exec tsc -p tsconfig.tests.json --noEmit`: exit 0.
   - Not run: the full `pnpm ci:ut` layer (same `e2e-auth.js` limitation), the real E2E J5 (needs a paid Nightly / live stack), and the mocked J3 E2E (needs bubblewrap, not installed on this VM). The new unit tests are the verification for this evidence-only change.
6. **Diff scope:** 5 files, +137/−7. No derived files, snapshots, or docs to regenerate; no docs pin the old reason text.
7. **Risks checked and excluded:**
   - Secrets: `setup.error` is already credential-redacted at the source (`redactNetworkError` in `environment-store.ts:1458`, and `failSetup` is the sole writer of both `setup.error` and component errors), and the journey report redacts the BLOCKED reason (`journey-report.ts:377-380`). Appending the transcript adds no new secret channel.
   - Bound: both transcripts pass through the 1200-char bound; worst case ≈ 2.5k chars total in the reason.
   - Micromamba: a micromamba failure reaches the reason via `setup.error` (its failure is terminal for that attempt, so `lastSetupError` is the micromamba error); no information is lost by not appending `components.micromamba.error` separately.
   - The differing-conda branch is defensive: `failSetup` writes the same string to both fields, so today they are identical or the component one is null. It is kept (bounded, tested) so a future store change reporting a distinct per-component transcript still surfaces it.
   - Known limitation (follow-up, not this PR): a multi-line reason renders imperfectly in the journey report — `journey-report.ts:458` blockquotes only the first line in `report.md`, and the HTML `<blockquote>` collapses line breaks. No content is lost in either format; fixing the renderer touches shared report code and is left as a follow-up.

Refs #1239.

## E2E user journeys

- J5 (real E2E): BLOCKED / not run — needs a paid Nightly run / live stack with real model credentials; the new unit tests are the verification for this evidence-only change.
- J3 (mocked E2E): BLOCKED / not run — needs bubblewrap and a running stack, neither available on this VM.
- Unit: `test/helpers/environment-setup.unit.ts` 17/17 pass (see Validation above).

## Release

Release category: release:internal
User impact: none — test helpers/specs only; the next Nightly run's BLOCKED reason will carry the setup failure transcript.
Compatibility and migration: none

---

Note for the maintainer: I cannot apply the `release:internal` label myself (403), and I did not use auto-merge. Could you please add the `release:internal` label and add this PR to the merge queue when it is ready?

1240.title: fix(e2e): include setup error transcript in BLOCKED reason

1242.author: ink999107
1242.body:
The add-model dialog's model-name field laid 刷新列表 inside the input, which forced 104px of right padding and cut the placeholder to `例如 deepseek-cha`; the action read as part of that grey text. The fetched listing was an absolutely positioned menu inside the dialog, so the dialog's `overflow-y: auto` clipped it after its first row, it drew over 测试连接/保存, and the input's `onBlur` closed the menu as soon as its scrollbar was touched.

## The model-name field

- 刷新列表 is a bordered button beside the field, with an icon and a spinner; the input keeps the full placeholder and only reserves room for the caret.
- The listing is portalled to `<body>` with its own fixed geometry: up to 320px tall, it flips above the field when there is not enough room below, has a visible thin scrollbar, and follows the dialog when that scrolls.
- It opens from a click on the field or the caret, and closes on Escape, an outside pointer, Tab or a choice. It intentionally no longer closes on blur, so dragging the scrollbar works.
- Keyboard: arrows, Home/End, Enter, Escape. Opening starts on the saved value; typing filters and an empty state says the name can still be typed.
- A successful 刷新列表 opens the list itself. A square surface-coloured backing behind the rounded menu stops its corner notch from showing a sliver of the label behind it.

## Provider and protocol choosers

- Both now use the app's `ListSelect` instead of a native `<select>`, whose popup is drawn by the OS and cannot take this dialog's type, spacing or hover states.
- Rows are 36px with a hover tint, a check on the current value and a visible scrollbar; the saved value is scrolled into view on open.
- Escape is claimed in the capture phase, so it closes only the list, not the dialog and the settings surface behind it.

## Dialog shell

- A one-line hint under the title, 36px fields with a blue focus ring, verdict banners for pass/fail, and 取消 demoted to the far side of a divided action row, with 测试连接 and 保存 together.

## Validation

- `pnpm --filter @sciencediscovery/desktop typecheck`: pass.
- desktop unit suite on `31904ed5` (upstream main base): 1192 passed, 0 failed, 128 suites.
- desktop `vite build`: pass.
- desktop mocked E2E on `31904ed5`: the changed journeys pass — the model listing test (including the real-pointer caret close and the Escape-after-padding-click case) and the setup wizard journey (including the 刷新列表 height/font/border comparison). A wider run of `settings.spec.ts` + `settings-interactions.spec.ts` + `setup.spec.ts` on `c534f941` was 34 passed / 1 failed; that failure is 技能 › "a card opens to the skill's source, version and file count" (expected `内置 · v1.0.0 · 4 个文件`, received `指令没有读到指令。v1.0.0 · 4 个文件`), which fails identically on unmodified upstream/main `59d05aa7`, so it is pre-existing and outside this diff.
- CodeCheck (GitCode): the unresolved-findings export named two identical-implementation findings in this PR's tests; both are fixed at `6b8f76c1` by sharing `boxStyle` and `fetchButton`. No product code changed.

- Repo layers `pnpm ci:ut` / `ci:st` / `ci:e2e`: **BLOCKED on this host**. `ci:ut` completes `pnpm install` and `pnpm build` but stalls in `uv sync --project services/paper --locked` (the first attempt was killed after 10 minutes at the same step; the retry is still in that step). No test in those layers ran locally. GitHub Actions will run them; this diff touches no Python and no service code.

## E2E user journeys

**PASS** for the changed dialog — tested commit `31904ed5`, desktop Chromium against the mocked API.

Command: `PLAYWRIGHT_BROWSERS_PATH=<browsers> apps/desktop/e2e/node_modules/.bin/playwright test --config apps/desktop/e2e/playwright.config.ts settings.spec.ts settings-interactions.spec.ts setup.spec.ts`

- 添加模型 → 服务商类型 → expected an app-drawn list and one Escape per layer → actual: the list opens, DeepSeek fills the base URL, Escape closes only the list while the dialog and settings stay.
- First-run wizard model step → test → continue: expected the shared form to work in its wizard host → actual: passes.
- Counts: 34 passed, 1 failed (the pre-existing 技能 card case above, reproduced on the base), 0 blocked at this level.

1243.author: ink999107
1243.body:
The hub currently publishes and downloads, but a merged PR is the only way to add anything: there is no account, no upload, no review, no version history, and no way to keep an asset invisible until someone approves it. This adds the backend those four requirements need, modelled on the openJiuwen Agentic Hub reference, and the two pieces that make the switch a deployment step rather than a rewrite: an importer for the existing catalogue and one build-time switch in the site.

**Stacked on #1225.** The static hub is that pull request. This branch is based on its head, so until #1225 merges the diff below includes it; the backend itself is the four commits on top.

## The service (`services/hub-api`)

FastAPI + SQLAlchemy. The reference establishes the shape: an asset row carrying what the site shows, a version row carrying what a download serves, review state on the version, and `public_latest_version` deciding what is listed. This keeps that contract and differs where our data does:

- Five asset kinds in one lifecycle (`skill`, `team`, `specialist`, `connector`, `session`) instead of six per-type models.
- No plugin-specific schema validation; a version is a zip or `.sdresearch` plus an inventory. The server validates what a server must: the 50 MiB cap measured on the bytes rather than `Content-Length`, path traversal, absolute paths, backslashes, encrypted and duplicate entries, and an uncompressed-size ceiling. Every entry's size and sha256 become the manifest the Files tab renders.
- Stateless HMAC session tokens instead of a Redis-backed store, and scrypt password hashing, so the database is the only stateful dependency.
- The response envelope (`{code, message, data}`) and the public paths (`/api/v1/assets`, `/api/v1/artifacts/{id}`) match the reference, so a client can be repointed.

Endpoints: register/login/me (`{id, username, display_name, role}` payloads), asset list/detail/create/update, version upload/list/detail, the files listing with `with_content`, `GET /api/v1/artifacts/{id}?version=` returning a presigned URL, and an admin review queue with approve/reject. Registration closes after the first account; that account is the administrator, and later accounts come from `POST /api/v1/auth/users`.

## Storage and access

One private bucket; keys are `assets/<kind>/<publisher>/<asset>/<version>/<filename>` composed in one function. Nothing is anonymously readable: a download resolves through the API, which checks visibility and returns a URL that expires (`HUB_PRESIGN_SECONDS`, default 10 minutes). External skill ids are paths (`chemistry_and_materials/real_world_workstations/…`), so storage keys validate the id segment by segment and the API routes it with a path converter.

## The importer

`scripts/import_catalog.py` reads the exporter's `catalog.json` and writes the same data into the database and the bucket. It preserves catalogue ids, verifies each artifact against the catalogue's sha256 before uploading, wraps the single-file specialists and connectors in a one-entry archive while checking the digest against the file rather than the wrapper, marks each imported version approved, and is idempotent. `--dry-run` validates without writing.

## The site

One build-time switch: with `VITE_HUB_API_BASE=/api/v1` the download button asks the API for a short-lived URL before navigating, which is what a private bucket requires. If that call fails the anchor still points at the catalogue URL, so a static deployment behaves exactly as before. Listing, README and the Files tab still come from `catalog.json`.

## CI

`hub-api.yml` runs the service's tests and builds its image on changes under `services/hub-api`.

## Validation

- `python -m pytest` in `services/hub-api`: **13 passed**. Covers registration and its closing, login, tampered tokens, administrator-created accounts, upload → pending → hidden, approval → listed and downloadable with matching sha256, rejection, owner-only uploads, the Files listing and text preview, path-shaped ids through the `%2F` encoding the site sends, the size/traversal/non-zip refusals, and the importer end to end (including idempotence and a checksum mismatch).
- `python -m scripts.import_catalog --dry-run` against the real catalogue: 387 assets, 385 versions, two session packages skipped because their `.sdresearch` files are not in the site tree.
- `pnpm --filter @sciencediscovery/hub typecheck` and `pnpm --filter @sciencediscovery/hub build`, with and without the API switch.

## E2E user journeys

**PASS on a local stack** — this host's MySQL 8.0 (container) + the service + the built site + the real OBS bucket, driven over HTTP and in Chromium. Not yet on a deployment host; that is the next step when one is available.

- Import into MySQL and OBS: `assets: 387 created`, `versions: 385 imported`, the two sessions above skipped. Keys land under `assets/<kind>/…` in the bucket.
- Chromium, `http://127.0.0.1:8612/site/skills/antibody-design`: the button's static `href` is `/site/packages/antibody-design-1.0.0.zip`; the click issues `GET /api/v1/artifacts/antibody-design?version=1.0.0` and the presigned URL serves 109171 bytes whose sha256 equals the catalogue's.
- Chromium, the path-id external skill `astronomy/astronomical_analysis/astropy`: the click issues `GET /api/v1/artifacts/astronomy%2Fastronomical_analysis%2Fastropy?version=snapshot-20261117` and the download's sha256 equals the catalogue's.
- HTTP, not the test client: login as the administrator, create an asset, upload (`201`, `pending`), approve (`200`), download; the bytes match, and the test asset and object were removed afterwards.
- The bucket is private: an unsigned `GET` of an object returns `403`, as does a bucket listing.

Building the real service against OBS surfaced two fixes that are in this branch: boto3 1.36+ adds a CRC32 trailer that OBS rejects (`XAmzContentSHA256Mismatch`), so checksum calculation is `when_required`; and asset ids longer than 64 characters (88 is the maximum, 84 exceed 64) needed wider columns and path-aware routes.

The host clock is 28 minutes ahead, which SigV4 rejects. The smoke tooling compensates for a drifting development host; the service deliberately does not, and its README says the deployment host must run NTP.

## Release

Release category: `release:feature` — the GitHub label is pending a maintainer, because this account has no write access to the upstream repository's labels.

User impact: accounts, uploads, version history and review can exist behind the hub; downloads can come from a private bucket through short-lived URLs.

Compatibility and migration: none for existing behaviour. The static exporter and the public-read publishing workflow are unchanged; the site only changes shape when built with `VITE_HUB_API_BASE`. The database is new and its schema is created at startup; the importer is the migration path from `catalog.json`.

1243.title: feat(hub): add the backend for accounts, uploads and signed downloads

1244.author: ink999107
1244.body:
The desktop transcript draws a "Connecting to the local service…" strip under the run line while the session's configuration requests are being read. A live run re-reads that list constantly: the two-second poll does it, and every run-status or tool-status change does it through the refresh key. The hook turned its loading state on for each of those reads, so on a session with no configuration cards the strip appeared and disappeared below "Planning the next step" every couple of seconds. The strip has padding and a bottom border, so each appearance resized the transcript, and the resize observer re-pinned the scroll to the bottom — the flash readers saw while the model was still planning.

## What changed

`useConfigurationRequests` now keeps two separate states:

- `loading` means the first read of this session is still out. It is the only state that draws the connecting strip.
- `reading` means any read is in flight. The poll throttle uses it, so slow reads are still allowed to finish without the poll claiming a new connection.

Background refreshes no longer touch `loading`, and `merge` only repaints when the request list actually changed. A poll that read the same list renders nothing at all. A failed background read still repaints, because the retry line it adds is a visible change — previously that repaint came from the loading transition that is now gone.

The regression test mounts a session that is running with no configuration cards, resolves the first read, then fires a refresh-key change and asserts `loading` stays false across the second read.

## Validation

Typecheck on commit 837352eb: `tsc -p apps/desktop/tsconfig.json --noEmit` — pass.

The new and existing hook tests: `tsx --test tests/configuration-requests.test.tsx` — 9 passed, 0 failed.

Local CI layers on commit 837352eb (Linux/amd64):

| Layer | planned | executed | passed | failed | skipped |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| UT | 7761 | 7730 | 7710 | 20 | 0 |
| ST | 63 | 63 | 62 | 1 | 0 |
| mocked E2E | 188 | 183 | 173 | 10 | 0 |

The UT baseline on unmodified `upstream/main` (59d05aa7) is planned 7760 / executed 7729 / passed 7713 / failed 16. (The one extra planned case is this change's regression test.)

- 16 of the 20 UT failures are byte-for-byte the same cases on the baseline: `jiuwenswarm-agent` (4, `unable to open database file`), `launcher serve` (5) and `launcher source-evolve` (5, owned stack exits before becoming healthy), `sandbox-network` (`bwrap: Unknown option --disable-userns`, host bubblewrap 0.6.1), `start-stack-lock` (the "pre-fix body must fail" meta-test does not reproduce the interrupt).
- The 4 UT failures that appear only in the fix run — `remote-compute-prune` (3, `/proc/*/exe` unreadable in this container, pruning exits -1) and `shell-executions` (timing: receipt observed as `running`) — pass when rerun on the same commit: 13/13 and 62/62 respectively. They are host-state flakiness, not this change.
- The single ST failure is `test/api/evolve-distribution.test.ts`: `fetch-runtime.mjs` cannot download the pinned Python runtime from GitHub releases (`fetch failed`). It is a network failure before any product assertion, and the same test also fails on the `upstream/main` baseline (61/63 there; the baseline additionally flaked once on `codex.st.test.ts`, which passed on this branch).

E2E was first blocked because port 4410 is owned by another stack on this host, then rerun on free ports 4710 / 4711 / 17774. Its 10 failures are all environment failures and do not reach the changed code:

- `journey-desktop-configuration` en and zh — the desktop Vite server could not bind port 4178 (`Error: Port 4178 is already in use`; another stack owns it), so the page never reached the configuration card.
- `journey-prepare-environment` — `BLOCKED: managed Python base is not ready (failed: micromamba setup failed)`.
- `journey-compact-process` — the shared E2E data directory still held a writable Skill library `project-skills`, which the fresh isolation state cannot reproduce; the harness says to reset the data directory.
- `issue-143-proxy-settings` (3) — the page stayed at `/?panel=open` and never created the session the journey navigates to, a knock-on of the shared global state in that group.
- `journey-custom-mcp` — the custom server row was absent after the same group's earlier failures.
- `journey-reviewer-upload-lifecycle` — the mocked run did not reach a terminal state (`running` after the wait).

The flicker itself is a timing behaviour that no existing mocked journey asserts on; the regression test covers it at the state level. A browser-level assertion for "the strip never appears during a live run" would need a dedicated journey and is not added here.

## E2E user journeys

FAIL (environment-blocked, see above), on commit 837352eb, browser subset against a local mocked stack on ports 4710/4711/17774, pinned Chromium; 188 planned, 183 executed, 173 passed, 10 failed, 0 skipped. The changed path — a running session with no configuration cards — is exercised on every run of the mocked chat journeys, which passed; the two journeys that would render the configuration card failed before the page loaded, on a port bind, so they did not observe this change either way.

## Release
Release category: `release:fix`

The GitHub label could not be applied from this account (no write access on the upstream repository), so `release:fix` is pending a maintainer. The category is recorded here as well.

User impact: the transcript no longer flashes under "Planning the next step" while a session with no configuration cards is running.
Compatibility and migration: none.

---

Fixes #1247.

1246.author: zhaochen39
1246.body:
This change addresses intermittent real-E2E gate failures and makes recovered failures visible. Failed-case retries are enabled only for the paid nightly and release profiles. A completed model stream can also still be used when the transport closes after a valid terminal marker.

## Retry failed real-E2E cases in nightly and release profiles

- Retry every executed `FAIL` or `PROVIDER_FAULT` case at most once for the `daily` and `release` profiles.
- Keep `pr` and `merge` profiles fail-fast at the case level without a second execution.
- Store retry evidence in an isolated directory and preserve the first attempt in `firstAttempt` and `retryHistory`.
- Use the retry result for the final gate only when the retry report is present and passes.
- Record and display `passed_after_retry` in the shared-plan summary. A failed or missing retry report keeps the gate failed.
- Preserve first-attempt runner-level errors so an after-all or collection failure cannot be masked by a recovered case.

## Recover completed model streams

- Accept an already completed OpenAI Chat Completions stream when the connection resets after a valid `finish_reason`.
- Preserve completed tool-call results without replaying terminal tool deltas.
- Keep tool-call parameter validation intact and retain transport diagnostics for incomplete streams.

## Stabilize the SRBench journey and diagnostics

- Accept a PUCT search that finishes early with the server-reported `stopReason: target_reward`, using the run's own scorecard decision instead of reconstructing a client-side threshold.
- Attach real-request setup diagnostics to the journey evidence.
- Restore provider-fault summary coverage and remove the obsolete outage-probe constant.
- Update the CI documentation to describe the profile-gated retry contract.
- Use one retry-recovery count as the source for both the camelCase artifact field and the existing `passed_after_retry` compatibility field.

## Validation

- Before the review follow-up changes, model package tests reported `159 passed, 0 failed, 0 skipped`.
- Before the review follow-up changes, provider-fault and retry-gate tests reported `25 passed, 0 failed, 0 skipped`.
- The follow-up changes were not locally tested, as requested. The complete `ci:l1`, `ci:ut`, `ci:st`, and `ci:e2e` slices were also not rerun locally.
- GitHub Actions is the validation path for the updated head. Live nightly and release E2E remain remote-only.

## E2E user journeys

**BLOCKED for local live execution.** The updated head is `b7f71f39`.

| Journey | Expected outcome | Actual outcome |
| --- | --- | --- |
| A `daily` or `release` real-E2E case fails once and passes on one complete retry | The final gate is `PASS`, while the first failure and retry history remain available and the summary shows the recovery | The retry contract and summary coverage were added. The updated code was not locally tested. |
| A `pr` or `merge` real-E2E case fails | The first failure remains the final result and no second execution starts | Profile-gating coverage was added. The updated code was not locally tested. |
| An OpenAI Chat stream reaches a valid terminal marker before transport reset | The completed answer remains usable and terminal tool-call data is not duplicated | Existing model completion coverage passed before the review follow-up changes. |
| An SRBench search ends with `stopReason: target_reward` before the expansion target | The journey accepts the server's successful early-stop decision | The client now trusts the reported stop reason. The updated journey was not locally run. |

## Release

Release category: `release:fix`

User impact: Limits flaky-case retries to nightly and release validation, exposes recovered failures in gate summaries, accepts valid server-reported SRBench early completion, and preserves completed model responses during late transport disconnects.

Compatibility and migration: None.
