Fix the merge-queue UT flake reported in #1245. The case "an immediate bubblewrap failure is reported instead of leaving the execution pending" in `services/runner/src/npu-devices.test.ts` used a 500 ms fake seccomp close plus a 250 ms wall-clock assertion. On a loaded 4-worker/4-vCPU UT slice that assertion failed with `exit was reported only after 296ms; the seccomp close must not be awaited`, because the measured span also includes load-sensitive startup work.

The case now observes event order instead of time. `closeSeccompFilter` sets `closeStarted` and waits on a gate that the test releases only after `executePython` settles. The test asserts `closeStarted === true` and `closeFinished === false`, releases the gate, and waits for the close. `execTimeoutMs` remains 1 500 ms, so an implementation that awaits the close rejects with the execution timeout instead of passing. A `context.after` hook releases the gate when an assertion fails. The comment above the gate states that timeout-rejection path; its previous wording named the stderr assertion, which is not evaluated on that path.

The change is test-only: `services/runner/src/executor.ts:1310` still calls `void closeFilter(...)` and is unchanged.

Verified on candidate tree 277fbfc0885c2f933213663c58daeaf9e276a4cd (head 15d761e4cf0942d4798ded5bd3246aae183fab67 on top of PR head 11a1c1e1):

1255.author: yuanzhou75
1255.body:
Closes #1253

The desktop MCP settings page could only edit a server that already existed: the form's sole entry was `setDraft(draftOf(server))`, and `emptyDraft()` was unreachable fallback filler. "Add my own MCP server" was impossible in the desktop app — which is where the local stack runs, and therefore where a `stdio` server would be launched. This brings the page to the web client's parity on the already-present routes; nothing on the server, the schema or the packaging moves.

## What the page can do now

**添加服务器.** The existing form opens empty (`emptyDraft()`) and saves with `POST /api/mcp/servers` (no id). The draft starts switched off, as an imported server does, and is reached by agents only once the user has read the test result and turned it on — testing it works while it is off, because the probe builds its own client. The created server is tested straight away — `POST /api/mcp/servers/:id/test` — and the dialog stays open with what the test found: the tool names, or the failure. That is the difference between finding a wrong command in the dialog and finding it at the next run. A refused save keeps the form and its fields on screen with the reason from the route.

**导入.** A `{"mcpServers": {…}}` spec is parsed and previewed as `name · transport · target`, then written **one request per server**. That is deliberate: `POST /api/mcp/servers/import` writes the whole spec or nothing and stops at the first name clash, so a spec of two servers would report one opaque error. Per-server requests give each entry its own outcome (`已添加` / `失败：…`) and let the valid half land.

**工具.** Each custom row expands to a read-only list of the tools the server reports (`name` and description). This is what tells the user whether adding it was worth it; the row already carried the count.

**未授权 / 授权 / 取消授权 / 清除授权.** A server whose `authorization.state` is not `authorized` says so — `未授权`, or `授权已过期` for `expired` — instead of looking broken next to a `已连接` status. 授权 opens a popup and posts `POST …/oauth/start` with this origin's callback URL (`/api/mcp/oauth/callback`), then navigates the popup to the URL the route minted; 取消授权 and 清除授权 call `…/oauth/cancel` and `…/oauth/clear` and re-read the list.

**Secrets stay unreadable.** The existing rule is untouched: a stored env/header value renders as an empty password field whose placeholder says it is stored, a rename without a value is refused before the write, and the new OAuth secret keeps the same `null`-means-keep semantics.

## Verification

- `tsc -p apps/desktop --noEmit`: clean.
- New suite `apps/desktop/tests/mcp-servers-create.test.tsx`: **11/11** — 添加服务器 opens an empty form, posts without an id, and starts the new server disabled, then names the tools its first test found; a refused create keeps the form open with the reason; saving with no name says the name is required; 导入 writes one request per server and reports each outcome (including the refused half's own sentence); the import preview reads the transport the way the route stores it; 编辑 after a create opens the row's own fields; a row awaiting consent is re-read until the grant lands and is then tested; 授权 detaches the popup and keeps the minted URL reachable when the popup is blocked; a stored env secret is never rendered back.
- Related existing suites (`mcp-discovery-refresh`, `settings-screens`): on this Windows host 5 pass, 0 fail, 2 skipped. The two skipped are `os:linux`-tagged and do not register on Windows, so they are reported as skipped rather than as passing — an earlier version of this section said "skipped by their platform tag" without saying which platform, which the review correctly found does not reproduce on Linux. Across the three files on this host: 13 tests, 11 pass, 0 fail, 2 skipped; CI `UT` (Linux) is green on `6edd132e` for the same files.
- Each fix above was mutation-checked: reverting it turns its own test red, and the file was restored afterwards.
- `vite build` (apps/desktop): succeeds, only the pre-existing chunk-size warning.
- `pnpm ci:l1`: not runnable on this host (the l1 profile targets `linux/amd64` and reports `executed: 0`), so CI is the word on it.

## Screenshots

Desktop renderer at this head, mock control plane, 1440×940, one browser per locale; the MCP routes are mocked, and every capture is taken after the assertion quoted beside it. The images live on `screenshots-1253`, not on this branch — the PR diff carries no binary.

1257.author: yuanzhou75
1257.body:
Closes #1252

## What this adds

An assistant turn that wrote files used to say nothing about them. The artifacts lived only in the right panel, grouped by Session, so a reader following the conversation had to work out which of them came from the answer in front of them — the panel answers "what does this research hold", not "what did this answer hand me".

The data already carried the link: a `ScientificArtifactVersion` records the turn that wrote it in `turnId`, which is the `SessionRun` the transcript draws, and `AssistantTurn` already had that run id. This PR reads that link and draws the result under the turn.

![A turn that wrote a report, a figure and a dataset](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/yuanzhou75/sciencediscovery/d4b3e32e6bc6a36c7f3b69a07a032d0e525f7c97/docs/screenshots/1252/1252-cards-zh.png)

Two cards to a line, each carrying the glyph and tint of the kind that wrote it — report, figure, dataset, structure, notebook, page, LaTeX, JSON, document, other. A row per file was a table of contents under every answer; a card is one file, and two of them fit beside each other without the next answer being pushed down the page. The width is fixed by `min(100%, 320px)` in the grid: the transcript column is about 716px, so two cards and the gap fit and a third does not. On a narrow window it collapses to one column rather than squeezing names to two characters:

![The same strip in a narrow window](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/yuanzhou75/sciencediscovery/d4b3e32e6bc6a36c7f3b69a07a032d0e525f7c97/docs/screenshots/1252/1252-cards-narrow.png)

Pressing a card opens **the right panel's own artifact view, at the version the card printed** — not the dialog, and not the newest version. Here the report is at v2 with `已更新`, and the panel opens on v2:

![Pressing a card opens it in the panel at that version](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/yuanzhou75/sciencediscovery/d4b3e32e6bc6a36c7f3b69a07a032d0e525f7c97/docs/screenshots/1252/1252-cards-preview.png)

Past five files the strip stops and offers the rest, which opens the panel's artifact group:

![Seven files: five cards and the door to the rest](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/yuanzhou75/sciencediscovery/d4b3e32e6bc6a36c7f3b69a07a032d0e525f7c97/docs/screenshots/1252/1252-cards-overflow.png)

English strings on the same three files:

![The same cards with English strings](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/yuanzhou75/sciencediscovery/d4b3e32e6bc6a36c7f3b69a07a032d0e525f7c97/docs/screenshots/1252/1252-cards-en.png)

## The rules, and why

**A version is attached by `version.turnId`, never by `executionRunIds`.** The schema states the rule: `SessionArtifactOutput` is assigned "to the visible top-level Run from `version.turnId`" (`packages/schema/src/artifact-provenance.ts`), and `apps/web/src/session/run-artifacts.ts` groups outputs the same way. `executionRunIds` names something else — the `ExecutionRun`, i.e. the code or shell execution that wrote the bytes — and never shares a value with the run id. The real shape is `{turnId: "run-source", executionRunIds: ["exec-source"]}` (`test/support/research-package.fixture.ts`).

**A child agent's version climbs to its run.** A subagent-produced version records the subagent as its `turnId`; the subagent records the turn that delegated it as `parentTurnId`. The walk follows that chain (children of children included) until it reaches a run the transcript holds. The lineage comes from the subagents already in the run states the conversation renders — no new request.

**A version the transcript cannot place is left out, not guessed at.** No `turnId` (an upload, a hand-registered file), a `turnId` that resolves to no run here, or a `parentTurnId` cycle: none of these is attached. Attributing by timestamp would turn project history into invented chat history; the version stays reachable from the panel's artifact list either way.

**One card per artifact, at the highest `version` ordinal — not the latest `createdAt`.** These two disagree exactly where it matters: an imported Session keeps the package's ordinals while `createdAt` can be the import time, so the newest timestamp may be an old version. The ordinal is the file's own lineage. A test pins this (`the ordinal wins over a later timestamp, which import reorders`).

**The card opens the version it names, not the newest one.** The card hands the panel the whole `SessionArtifactOutput` record, and the panel is matched on `version.id` — the identity, not the ordinal — so "the card says v3" and "the document shows v3" cannot drift apart even when the file has a v4 written by a later run. Pressing `v3` gives `v3`. The third screenshot shows it: the card is at v2 and the panel opens at v2.

**`已更新` comes from `baseVersionId` on the version the row points at.** Boundary worth stating: if a run created v1 and then wrote v2 in the same turn, v2 carries a `baseVersionId` and a file this turn created is marked 已更新. That is rare and accepted — the marker answers "did the last write derive from an earlier one", not "did this run create the artifact". Noted in the module.

**日志 has no kind of its own.** #1252 asks for logs to be folded; `ScientificArtifactKind` has ten values (`dataset | figure | html | json | latex | markdown | notebook | other | report | structure`) and no `log`. The run's intermediate output is `json`/`other`, so those two are the folded set. They sit behind the overflow card when the turn also produced something better, and are shown when they are all it produced — an empty strip reading "3 more" with nothing behind it reads as a bug.

**A later turn's version of the same file stays under that later turn.** Each turn shows the highest ordinal *it* wrote; a file amended by turn 2 still shows turn 1's version under turn 1. `limit` counts per run, not per Session.

**Nothing is drawn while the run is streaming.** The guard is the existing `run.terminal`, the same signal the rest of the transcript uses to settle a turn, rather than a second local heuristic. A list that grows and reshuffles under the reader while the run is still writing is worse than no list.

## Where the code is

- `apps/desktop/src/app/turn-artifacts.ts` — the selection: `ownerRunId` (the `turnId` → `parentTurnId` walk), kind order, the folded set, the five-row cap, and `turnArtifactsByRun`, which does the work once per `outputs`/lineage pair instead of once per turn.
- `apps/desktop/src/views/TurnArtifactStrip.tsx` — the cards, the per-kind glyphs, and the overflow tile.
- `App.tsx` → `Conversation.tsx` → `AssistantTurn.tsx` — `outputs={state.outputs}` down to each turn, `openArtifactPanel` for the overflow tile, and `previewTurnArtifact` — a stable callback (outputs and the panel's opener are read through refs) so the memoised transcript is not re-rendered by a tab switch — for the cards. `Conversation` builds the lineage from the runs and subagents it already renders and memoises the map on it and on `outputs`; `WorkspacePanel` already rebuilds its grouping on every render, and a per-turn scan would make typing in the composer cost O(turns × outputs).

## Two defects this PR fixes on itself

**The join was on the wrong field.** The first cut matched the turn's run id against `version.executionRunIds`. Those are different identifiers (see the first rule above), so on a real Session the strip would have been empty for every turn. Review caught it on `86d254ef`; the tests had not, because their fixtures set `executionRunIds` to the run id — a shape the backend never writes. The join is now on `turnId` with the subagent walk, and the fixtures use the real shape: `turnId` = the run, `executionRunIds` = a distinct execution id. A case pins the boundary directly (`a version whose executionRunIds happen to name a run is not attached by them`): with a join on `executionRunIds` added back, it fails (`16 tests, 15 pass, 1 fail`); without it, 16/16.

**The row order fell back to the version id.** That tiebreak is there so that picking one file's newest version is deterministic when two of its versions share an ordinal — but between two *different* files the ids always differ, so it always fired and the name comparison after it could never run. Seven reports written in one turn came out `7, 6, 5, 4, 3`. The order now falls back to the name, and a test pins it: with the id-ordered sort restored, `files of one kind and one version are listed by name, not by id` fails; with the fix, it passes.

## Verification

- `apps/desktop` `tsc -p tsconfig.json --noEmit`: clean.
- `tsc -p tsconfig.tests.json --noEmit` (repo root): clean.
- `pnpm --filter @sciencediscovery/desktop test`: **1270/1270**, no failures.
- New cases: `turn-artifacts.test.ts` (the `turnId` join and its `executionRunIds` boundary, no turn id, an unknown turn id, the subagent walk including nesting and a cycle, one row per artifact, a later turn's version staying under that turn, ordinal-over-timestamp, kind order, folding, the cap, name order, the by-run map) and `turn-artifact-strip.test.tsx` (no artifacts draws nothing; a streaming run draws nothing and a terminal one does; a card previews the exact `version.id` it prints rather than the newest; every card carries its kind's glyph and kind-tinted tile; five cards plus the 还有 2 个 tile opening the panel).
- Mutation checks: with `run.terminal` replaced by `true`, the streaming case fails; with the join on `executionRunIds` restored, the boundary case fails; with the id-ordered sort restored, the name-order case fails. Each passes once restored.

**What this does not prove.** Screenshots were captured against a Vite dev server serving this branch, with the desktop L2 mock answering `/api/**` — the same mock the desktop e2e specs use. Their fixtures now follow the real version shape (`turnId` = run, `executionRunIds` = a separate execution id, taken from `test/support/research-package.fixture.ts`), but they are synthetic: no real model and no real catalog wrote them. That is exactly how the first cut's wrong join slipped past both the tests and the screenshots, so a reviewer should treat the real-stack check as still owed. I could not run one here.

1257.title: feat(desktop): show what each assistant turn produced

1258.author: yuanzhou75
1258.body:
Closes #1254

## What was wrong

`main` carried **`0.4.1`**, a version no release has. The only 0.4.x release is **`v0.4.0-rc1`**, and the planned next one is `v0.4.0` (#1198). The number got there from a one-line edit inside an unrelated MCP fix (`#1197` / `65299d1e`):

```diff
-  "version": "0.4.0",
+  "version": "0.4.1",
```

That field is not a label. It names the Windows installer through `artifactName`, and it becomes the exe's `FileVersion` / `ProductVersion` — the "Apps & features" line a support conversation quotes. So an installer built from `main` advertised a release that does not exist, and nothing in CI noticed, because no workflow reads the field.

The same drift left two other things behind: both README badges said `Release-0.4.0` and linked `releases/tag/v0.4.0`, **which 404s**, and the NSIS syntax-check stub still said `0.4.0`.

## What this changes

**1. `main` goes back to the release line, with one spelling per place it is legal.**

| Place | Value | Why |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `application/package.json` `version` | `0.4.0-rc1` | SemVer — what electron-builder and electron-updater need |
| `application/electron-builder.yml` `artifactName` | `ScienceDiscovery-0.4.0.rc1-win-x64-setup.${ext}` | the dot form is a *file name*; `0.4.0.rc1` is not a valid version (`semver.valid()` is `null`) |
| `README.md`, `README_zh.md` | badge `0.4.0.rc1` → `releases/tag/v0.4.0-rc1` | the tag that actually exists |
| `application/build/nsh-syntax-check-stub.nsi` | `!define VERSION "0.4.0.rc1"` | same as the release branch |

This is the repo's own documented policy, written in `scripts/package-sd-windows.sh:59-61`: the dot spelling is not legal SemVer, so `package.json` takes the hyphen form and `artifactName` is pinned to the literal; at GA the version returns to `X.Y.Z` and `artifactName` goes back to `${version}`.

**2. Every payload now records the version it claims.**

`resources/version.json` carried `repoCommit` and `builtAt` but not the version, and `repoCommit` degrades to `"unknown"` when the tree has no git metadata — which is how one build came to report nothing at all. The version is one read of the shell's own `package.json`, the same file electron-builder takes its number from, so the two cannot disagree:

```json
{ "repoCommit": "…", "appVersion": "0.4.0-rc1", "builtAt": "…" }
```

**3. A version bump is now a release change, and CI enforces it.**

New `scripts/check-release-version.mjs`, run inside the **L1 job** (already required, so no new check to wire into `merge-gate`). When `application/package.json`'s `version` moves in a pull request, both must hold:

- the title starts with **`chore(release):`**, and
- **every** place the release is spelled carries the **new** number — the NSIS stub and both READMEs (badge dot form **and** `v<version>` tag link), and the artifact name as the dot-spelled literal for a pre-release or `${version}` for a final release, matching the policy in `scripts/package-sd-windows.sh`.

Either alone would be a door: a title is a password anyone can type, and a file set alone lets a functional PR launder a bump by nudging a README line. Together they describe `#1147`, the shape every release is supposed to take. "Carries the new number", not "was touched", is the half that matters in practice: touching `electron-builder.yml` while leaving `ScienceDiscovery-0.4.0.rc1-…` in place is the original defect wearing a release title. The version is also rejected outright if it is not SemVer-shaped, which catches the dot spelling with the form to use instead.

It lives in `.ci/release-version.mjs` and is computed by the **policy job** through `.ci/tier-policy.mjs`, because that job is already the diff-aware one — `fetch-depth: 0` and `changed-paths.mjs` are pre-existing — and it is the only place that can read the version the PR moved *from*. Its cases carry the same `category:ut` tags as every other `.ci/*.test.mjs`, so the shared plan collects, selects and counts them. **No workflow file changes at all**: not a step in `ci.yml`, not a job in the graph, not an L1 checkout depth. Only pull requests are checked — a push to `main` and the merge queue re-verify a commit whose PR already answered. `.ci/README.md` describes the rule next to the job that enforces it, including that a violation stops the run before L1.

## Verification

Driven through the policy job's own entry point, with a real `pull_request` payload and a real base commit:

| Case | Result |
| --- | --- |
| this PR, release title | **pass** (`rc=0`), policy outputs written |
| the same tree, `fix(mcp):` title | **fail** — the title |
| a bump to `0.5.0` with the metadata left at `0.4.0.rc1` | **fail** — names each file and each missing spelling |
| a `push` event | **pass** — not checked; the pull request already answered |

Unit cases: `.ci/release-version.test.mjs`, **18/18** — the unchanged tree, the release change, the **GA shape** (macro accepted, so #1198 can ship while following the policy), a pre-release that leaves the macro in place (still rejected: the macro cannot spell the dot form), the title-only door, the stale-metadata drift, one file behind being named alone, the dead prefix, the dot spelling, an unreadable file, `dotForm`, SemVer shapes, a guard that every declared requirement is one the checker implements, the policy verdict for a pull request versus a push/merge group, the wiring call, and the checkout read covering every metadata file — which caught a real defect on the way in: the mapping still destructured the old entry objects and crashed on `undefined`.

Other checks on this tree:

- `.ci/*.test.mjs` — the whole selftest, including this PR's cases and the contract test that reads the job graph: **173/173**. `node .ci/test-selector.mjs check` → `CI test catalog OK: 6 cases, 20 tags, 4 layers`.
- `scripts/*.test.mjs`: 121 pass, 3 fail — `check-doc-links`, `component-boundaries` and a race-contract case. All three fail **identically at the base commit `a117ae9`** in a worktree without `node_modules`, with `ERR_MODULE_NOT_FOUND` for `markdown-it` and `@babel/parser`. They are missing dependencies in this checkout, not regressions; CI installs them.
- Not run here: `pnpm --dir application dist` (needs the full Windows provisioning chain) and `pnpm docs:lint` (needs `markdownlint-cli2`). The README change is one badge URL; the lint config enables only MD001/012/031/040/045, none of which a link edit touches.

## What this does not do

The issue's fourth suggestion — surfacing the build identity in an About window — is **not** included; it is a new UI surface and was left out deliberately. `version.json` is the identity for now, which is what makes "which build is this?" answerable without the version. Suggested as a separate change if it is wanted.

`repoCommit` still falls back to `"unknown"` instead of failing the build: failing would break packaging from a source tarball, and the issue lists that as a decision rather than a defect.

1259.author: zhaochen39
1259.body:
Add an on-demand package profile to the CI workflow so maintainers can build and download distribution artifacts without running the test-tier jobs. This pull request uses the exact commit from `openJiuwen-ai/sciencediscovery:codex/l5-biomnibench-da-four-cases`.

## Package selection

- `linux-windows` (default) builds the two native Linux single-file packages and then the Windows x64 installer with their Runner SEA artifacts.
- `macos` builds Apple Silicon DMG and ZIP artifacts with ad-hoc signing.
- `all` starts Linux and macOS in parallel and starts Windows once the Linux Runner SEA inputs are ready.

The profile runs L1 and reports a separate `package-gate` check. The checks cover required job results and expected installer files before artifact upload.

## Validation

- Previous validation of this change reported 155 passed CI policy and workflow tests, 0 failed, and a clean `actionlint` result.
- At the request of the contributor, no local test suites were run for this PR submission. The full local test-tier results are not asserted here.

## E2E user journeys

1264.author: yuanzhou75
1264.body:
Closes #1262

## The defect

On a Session with no prior conversation, `/distill-session` still told the model to *"infer the reusable workflow from the complete prior Session conversation and execution history supplied above"*. There was nothing to infer from, and nothing told it to stop, so it went looking for the conversation: **28 `run_shell` calls walking the application's own data directory**, `turn: 32`, `totalTokens 88,824`, **0 drafts**, cancelled by hand after nine minutes.

The sibling `/skill-creator` branch in the same function already guards its missing input — *"No workflow description was supplied. Ask one concise question … do not create a generic Skill yet."* The distill branch had no equivalent.

## The fix

`skillAuthoringCommandPrompt` now takes `{ hasHistory }`. With no prior conversation the distill instruction becomes:

- **it says the Session has nothing to distil** — one short paragraph, in the reader's terms;
- **it asks one concise question** for what the Skill should capture (goal, inputs, outputs, checks) instead of inventing a generic one;
- **it forbids looking for the conversation**, naming the places the run actually wandered: the workspace, the application data directory, project and session folders, and shell commands;
- **it does not say `create_skill` yet**, so nothing half-formed lands in review.

`hasHistory` is "any user or assistant message", so a Session holding only runtime notices counts as empty. It defaults to **true**: a caller that does not know keeps the previous behaviour rather than silently refusing every distill.

The call site passes it from the messages already read for the prompt (`previousMessages`), so no extra read.

## Verification

`services/api/src/runs/index.test.ts`, **23/23**, and `tsc -p services/api --noEmit` clean.

The new case pins four things the prompt must say and the one instruction that must *not* be there — the inference sentence that caused the search. It also pins that the sibling `/skill-creator` path and the unknown-caller default are unchanged.

**Mutation check:** with the guard block removed, the case fails (`22 pass, 1 fail`); restored, `23/23`.

What that evidence does *not* claim: a unit test on a prompt cannot prove the model then makes no shell call — that needs a live run. What it does prove is that the instruction which sent the agent searching is gone and that the replacement forbids exactly the behaviour in the report.

## Deliberately not in this change

Two of the issue's suggestions are hardening around a cause this removes, and both need a decision rather than a default:

1. **A turn budget for authoring runs.** The main agent's budget is composed once per runtime (`profile.budget.maxModelTurns`), not per run, so a per-command cap means threading an override through that composition. It also needs a number, and picking one wrongly fails legitimate long distills of contentful Sessions — a product decision, not a default I should pick here.
2. **Disabling the action in the UI when the Session is empty.** `SkillManager`'s "Distill current Session" row (`apps/web/src/SkillManager.tsx:537`) already disables for "no session"; disabling for "no messages" needs the active Session's message count in that panel, which it does not receive today. That is a web-app plumbing change and a user-visible one, so it wants its own review.

Say the word and I will open a follow-up for either; I did not want to hold the fix behind them.

1267.author: yuanzhou75
1267.body:
Closes #1265

A provider that refuses `temperature` failed every run with the generic `semantic-error [181001]`, even though the same endpoint served another model fine. The request was always retryable — the field the provider named simply was not on the list of fields this client is willing to drop.

## Root cause

Verified on `main` `a117ae99`, not taken from the report:

- `services/api/src/agent-run/jiuwenswarm-model-gateway.ts:346` copies whatever sampling the swarm request carries into the model policy (`temperature`, `top_p`).
- `packages/model/src/client.ts:1574` (`:1594`, `:1614` for the OpenAI Responses and Anthropic variants) writes it into the provider request whenever the policy has it.
- The only 400 recovery is `rejectedControlFallback` (`packages/model/src/client.ts:938`). It gated on a hardcoded thinking-control regex — `/(thinking|reasoning|enable_thinking|chat_template_kwargs)/i` — so a detail that named only `temperature` never reached the per-field check, and `retryWithoutRejectedFields` returned `undefined`. The error was rethrown and the run ended.
- Two further reasons it would still have failed after adding the field to the list, both found while implementing:
  - `rejectedControlWording` (`:833`) is the vocabulary that proves a *parameter* was rejected. It read `unsupported|not supported|…|not allowed|not permitted|no such parameter`, and **`deprecated` was not in it** — which is exactly the word this provider used.
  - the candidate list the retreat is built from was the thinking controls only (`thinkingControlFields`, `:815`).

## What changed

- `temperature` and `top_p` join the retry candidates: `samplingControlFields` is added to a new `retryableControlFields`, which is what the pre-filter, the per-field wording check, the stripped retry, and the retry budget now use.
- `deprecated` and `no longer supported` are added to the rejection vocabulary, so "`temperature` is deprecated for this model" is recognised as a parameter rejection.
- The pre-filter no longer hardcodes thinking words: it asks whether the detail names any field this client can drop.
- The helpers that were thinking-only are renamed to say what they do now (`rejectedRetryableControlFields`, `carriedRetryableControls`, `withoutNamedFields`, `rememberRejectedControls`, …); their two consumers (`services/api/src/model-connectivity.ts`, and a doc reference in `completion.ts`) follow.
- The existing safety rule is untouched: a complaint about a control's **value** or the **state** it was sent in still strips nothing. `valueComplaintWording` keeps `when … is enabled/on/set` out of the rejection path, so "temperature is not supported when thinking is enabled" still fails the call rather than silently changing the requested mode.

## Tests

Two new cases in `packages/model/src/client.test.ts`, both with a stub server:

- **the fix**: the server answers `400 {"message":"`temperature` is deprecated for this model."}` when `temperature` is present and streams a normal turn when it is not. The first turn succeeds after the strip, `top_p` (which the 400 never named) survives, and a second turn sends no `temperature` — the rejection is remembered for the endpoint.
- **the guard**: a 400 saying "temperature is not supported when thinking is enabled" is still not a rejection — the call fails once and `temperature` is never stripped.

Mutation-checked, each revert turning the first case red and the file restored afterwards:

| Reverted | Result |
| --- | --- |
| sampling fields dropped from the retry list | `not ok — a 400 that deprecates a sampling field strips it…` |
| `deprecated` removed from the wording | same case red |
| pre-filter restored to the thinking-only regex | same case red |

## Verification

- `packages/model` `node --import tsx --test src/client.test.ts`: **49/49**, including the two new cases. Run on this Windows host with the suite's `os:linux` tag relaxed for the run only — the file declares `os:linux`, and the tag was restored before pushing, so CI is what reports the tagged run.
- `tsc -p packages/model/tsconfig.json --noEmit`: clean.
- `tsc -p services/api/tsconfig.json --noEmit`: clean.
- `tsc -p tsconfig.tests.json --noEmit` (repository root): clean.

## Deliberately not in this PR

- **The gateway keeps forwarding sampling to endpoints that never asked for it.** `jiuwenswarm-model-gateway.ts:346` could stop passing `temperature`/`top_p` for endpoints the user configured no sampling for, which would avoid the 400 entirely. That is a behaviour change for every provider — a model that currently receives the swarm's own defaults would stop receiving them — so it belongs in its own change with its own evidence. This PR fixes the failure, not the habit.
- **`services/evolve` is untouched.** `completion.py:116-121` already omits `temperature` by default for the same reason; that is a separate path and a separate fix history.
- **Where `temperature: 0.95` / `top_p: 0.95` come from is not claimed.** The swarm log states it produced those numbers, and `GET /api/models` on the reporting install carries no sampling fields, so it is a JiuwenSwarm/openJiuwen default — and that source is not in this repository. **I could not locate it**, so this description does not name one.

## Risk

The retry only happens after a `400` that names a field the request actually carried, and it stops as soon as the field is accepted. A provider that accepts `temperature` sees exactly the request it saw before.

1270.author: yuanzhou75
1270.body:
Closes #1265

## The defect

A provider that answers `400 … temperature is deprecated for this model` failed **every** run of that model, as `semantic-error` / `181001`, while another model on the same provider worked.

The streamed sender already had a strip-and-retry rule — strip exactly the field a 400 names, remember it for the endpoint once a stripped request succeeds — but it was **gated on the thinking-control names**, so this 400 never matched, the error was rethrown, and the run ended. `temperature` and `top_p` were in the request (the gateway copies whatever sampling the swarm sends into the model policy) and nothing could take them out.

## The fix

`temperature` and `top_p` join the thinking controls in one list of fields this sender knows how to do without, and the existing rule applies to them unchanged:

- **strip only what this 400 names** — a field the provider accepts is not dropped;
- **a value or state complaint is not a rejection** — `temperature must be between 0 and 2` and `temperature is not supported when thinking is enabled` still fail the request rather than silently changing the sampling the run asked for;
- **remember the field for the endpoint only after a stripped request succeeds**, so a fallback that itself fails (429, 5xx, timeout) proves nothing.

Two additions to the rejection wording: `deprecated`, and the `no longer supported/available/accepted` / `has been removed` phrasings, because *"is deprecated for this model"* is a rejection of the parameter, not of its value.

`rejectedThinkingControlFields` / `carriedThinkingControls` become `rejectedRequestFields` / `carriedRequestFields`, and the Settings connectivity probe (`services/api/src/model-connectivity.ts`) uses them, so the probe strips the same fields the sender does. Otherwise an endpoint whose streaming chat now works would still be reported broken by the probe.

## Verification

New `packages/model/src/sampling-fallback.test.ts`, three cases against a stub server:

| Case | Expected |
| --- | --- |
| `400 "temperature is deprecated for this model"` | retried without `temperature`, `top_p` kept, run continues, and the next turn sends no `temperature` |
| `400 "temperature must be between 0 and 2"` (with `param: "temperature"`) | **not** retried, still surfaces, and the field is not suppressed later |
| `400 "temperature is not supported when thinking is enabled"` | **not** retried — a state complaint is not a rejection |

**Mutation check:** with only the thinking controls in the list, case 1 fails (`2 pass, 1 fail`); restored, `3/3`.

Wider checks on this head: `packages/model` suite **162/162**; `model-connectivity.test.ts` **37/37**; `tsc -p tsconfig.tests.json --noEmit` and `tsc -p packages/model --noEmit` clean.

## What this does not do

The optional half of the issue — having the gateway stop forwarding sampling fields to endpoints whose models never asked for them — is not included. The client-side fallback is what makes such a model usable; suppressing the fields up front would be a second, independent decision about the swarm's defaults.

1272.author: yuanzhou75
1272.body:
Closes #1271

## The defect

The release-version gate read `application/package.json`'s `version` from the **working tree**. On a `pull_request` event the checkout is the **merge commit** — the head merged into the current base — while the comparison point came from `pull_request.base.sha`. A branch based on an older `main` was therefore compared against a tree it never wrote.

The incident: #1264, based on `222e7b06` (0.4.1) while `main` had moved to `0c3d4d52` (0.4.0-rc1, from #1258). The branch changes only `services/api/**`, but the merge tree carried `0.4.0-rc1`, so the gate reported a release change:

```
CI policy failed: application/package.json moves 0.4.1 -> 0.4.0-rc1, which is a
release change, but the title "fix(api): tell /distill-session it has nothing to
distil" does not start with "chore(release):".
```

`Select CI policy` fails first, so L1, UT and ST are skipped and `merge-gate` fails: **nothing on that head is validated**. Rebasing the same head onto current `main` made it pass, which is what identified the trigger as the stale base rather than the change.

Impact: every pull request whose branch is behind `main` is blocked before L1 by a rule it does not violate, and the only workaround — rebase — is undiscoverable and clears approvals.

## The fix

Both sides of the comparison now come from git objects:

```js
const headVersion = versionOf(showFile(head, VERSION_FILE));
const baseVersion = versionOf(showFile(base, VERSION_FILE));
...
const files = Object.fromEntries(RELEASE_METADATA.map(path => [path, readFromHead(path)]));
```

The working tree is not consulted at all. `pull_request.head.sha` is now required alongside `base.sha`, and its absence is a named error rather than a silent pass. The success line prints the version it accepted **from the head commit**, so a stale checkout can no longer make a green gate look like it verified something else:

```
release version OK: application/package.json at 0.4.1 (head 222e7b06a418)
```

## Verification

- **The incident, on real commits:** with the working tree at current `main` (`0.4.0-rc1`) and an event whose `base` and `head` are both `222e7b06` (`0.4.1`), the check now answers `release version OK … at 0.4.1 (head 222e7b06a418)`, rc=0. Before the change the same shape produced the failure above.
- **New regression case** (`a branch behind main is not a version bump (#1271)`): base and head both 0.4.1, and it asserts that no metadata file is even read. Plus `every metadata file is read from the pull request head, and the base from the base`, and a case asserting an event without `head.sha` is refused.
- **Mutation check:** restoring the working-tree read fails three cases, including the #1271 one (`22 pass, 3 fail`); restored, 25/25. So the regression case is load-bearing, not decorative.
- `.ci/*.test.mjs` — the whole selftest including the contract test: **178/178**.
- `node .ci/test-selector.mjs check`: catalog OK.

## Note on the gate's placement

This changes `.ci/tier-policy.mjs` only — no workflow file, no job in the graph. The placement of the gate itself was settled on #1258 (`policy` job) and is not reopened here.
1272.head: fix-1271-gate-head-tree
1272.title: fix(ci): read the release version from the pull request head, not the checkout

1273.author: yuanzhou75
1273.body:
Closes #1261

Confirming a distilled Session draft wrote the Skill into a Library and stopped there: the Skills page lists the Skill **catalog**, and no Library is enabled by default, so the Skill the user had just confirmed appeared nowhere and a Session could not select it. The content was never lost — it sat in a Library version — but from the user's side "summarize this session into a Skill" produced nothing.

## Root cause

Verified on `main` `baa66d05`, not taken from the report:

- `packages/specialist/src/skills.ts:1673` — `publishReviewDraft()` hands the reviewed bytes to an external publisher and deletes the draft. It never called `commitManaged()`, so nothing entered the Skill catalog.
- `services/api/src/http/index.ts:2485` — the confirm handler's `publish` callback commits a **Library version** only (`skillLibraryCatalog.commitVersion`).
- `/api/skills` is `skillCatalog.list()` (`services/api/src/http/index.ts:2456`); a Library is a separate catalog, and `enabledSkillLibraries` defaults to `[]` (`services/api/src/store.ts:348`), so a run imports nothing from it (`:1007`).
- The peer method `confirmReviewDraft()` (`packages/specialist/src/skills.ts:1638`) already did the full job — `commitManaged`, index entry, `saveIndex`, in-memory package. The Library path was the only one missing those three steps.

## What changed

`packages/specialist/src/skills.ts`

- The three installation steps move into one private `installReviewedDraft(loaded, provenance, baseRevision)`, called by **both** confirmation paths. The existing `SKILL_CONFLICT` guard for an already-installed Skill without a base revision comes with it, so a Library publication cannot silently overwrite revision 1 either.
- `publishReviewDraft()` installs the reviewed package into the catalog **after** the publisher succeeds, so a failed Library commit still leaves the draft intact (that ordering was already pinned by a test and is untouched).

Effect: a confirmed draft is now listed by `/api/skills` and selectable in a Session, with no client change — the Skills pages already render whatever the catalog returns. No UI file, no route shape and no Library behaviour was modified.

## Tests

`services/api/src/skills.test.ts`

- **New**: `a draft confirmed through a Library publication is also installed in the Skill catalog` — publishes through a stub publisher, then asserts the Skill is in the catalog at revision 1, appears in `list()`, the draft is consumed, and it survives a reload.
- **New**: `a Library publication refuses a colliding draft before it publishes anything` — installs the same id through an import while the draft is open, then asserts the publisher callback is never invoked and the draft survives.
- **Extended**: `keeps a reviewed Agent draft when its external Library publication fails` now also asserts the catalog stays empty when the publisher fails.

`services/api/src/server.test.ts` — the `swarm:required` case is renamed to `Agent-created Skill stays in draft until review publishes it to a Library and installs it in the catalog`; after the confirm it asserts `200`, the returned id, `currentRevision: 1`, presence in `/api/skills`, and that a Project created afterwards carries the id in `effective.enabledSkillIds`. The `404` **before** the confirm is untouched, so the two halves still bracket the confirm.

Both fixes are mutation-checked: dropping `installReviewedDraft` from `publishReviewDraft` turns the first case red; moving the guard back behind the publisher turns the collision case red.

## Verification

- `tsc -p packages/specialist`, `tsc -p services/api`, and `tsc -p tsconfig.tests.json` (root): all clean.
- `skills.test.ts` **27 tests / 26 pass / 1 fail** and `skill-library-api.test.ts` **4/4**, run on this Windows host with the files' `os:linux` tag relaxed for the run only (the tag is restored in the committed file). The single failure is `an imported script that declares an interpreter stays executable`, which asserts `stat().mode & 0o100` — NTFS has no POSIX mode bits. CI's Linux `UT` is the authority for it.
- `server.test.ts` cannot complete on this host: it reaches teardown and fails with `EBUSY … executions.sqlite-shm` while deleting its temp root, with no assertion error. I am not claiming a green run for it.

## Not in this PR

- **Auto-enabling the Library** and **listing Library-only Skills** were the alternative designs. Neither is needed once the confirmed package is in the catalog: the catalog is what both Skills pages already read, and a Skill installed there is selectable without touching `enabledSkillLibraries`. The Library keeps its role as the versioned archive.
1273.head: fix-1261-confirmed-skill-in-catalog
1273.title: fix(skills): install a confirmed draft in the Skill catalog, not only a Library

1279.author: yuanzhou75
1279.body:
The Idea Tree settings page had a **各阶段思考强度** block: five selects, one per stage (`发散` / `设计` / `评估` / `汇总` / `传播`), every one of them defaulting to `跟随模型`. Following the model is what a stage does when nobody picks a level, so the block only let a user move away from the behaviour they almost all keep. It is removed, and every stage now follows the research model's own thinking level.

Requested by the repository owner on 2026-11-21 (the block is redundant with the default). This does reverse part of #47, which introduced the per-stage effort, so a release note may want `release:breaking`.

Rebased twice on the same day as main moved under it: first onto `e4a7f8f4` (#1280, the save-row alignment in the same file), then onto `80fa5e14` (`3529a555` dropped the per-call token cap, which touched `idea_tree/research.py` and the same settings pane). Conflicts were resolved by keeping every other intent and dropping only this setting: the thinking group stays deleted, the save row keeps `settings-actions is-end`, `transport()` is `(system, payload)` with neither `max_tokens` nor `reasoning_effort`, and main's removal of the 「单次调用 token」 row is present in both frames. History was rewritten (`44a3b6e` → `6b0b2ae5` → `4b7b45a8`), so earlier review comments point at commits that no longer exist.

## What changes

The setting is removed end to end rather than hidden in one pane, because a stored map would otherwise keep overriding the model with no control left to clear it:

- **desktop pane** (`views/settings/IdeaTreeSettings.tsx`): the `各阶段思考强度` group, its per-stage selects, the `跟随模型` option list and the PUT field are gone; the pane still sends exactly the fields the API accepts. `各阶段思考强度`, `跟随模型` and the per-stage names leave both dictionaries, and the page description no longer promises per-stage effort (research scope and stage prompts remain).
- **schema** (`packages/schema/src/runtime-settings.ts`): `IdeaTreeThinkingRole`, `IdeaTreeRoleThinkingEfforts` and the three `roleThinkingEfforts` fields leave `IdeaTreeSettings`, `IdeaTreeSettingsDetails` and `UpdateIdeaTreeSettingsRequest`.
- **api store** (`services/api/src/store/settings.ts`): the map is no longer normalized, written or restored. A catalog row written by an older build drops it when it loads, and a client that still sends it does not fail its save — the field is simply not carried.
- **evolve engine** (`vendor/idea_tree`): `Settings` no longer takes the field, `role_effort` is gone, and the stage call neither asks for an effort nor a per-call ceiling, so a request is exactly the model profile's own.
- **docs** (`docs/{en,zh}/reference/runtime-behavior.md` and `docs/{en,zh}/reference/cli.md`): both now describe the Reviewer as the only role with its own effort, so no reference still advertises the retired setting.

Nothing else on the pane moves: template, exploration intensity, score direction, depth, nodes, the token cap, the stage prompts and the save row are untouched, and the pane writes the same request shape.

## Screenshots

**Component-level render, not a full application journey.** The real `IdeaTreeSettings` component mounted with a stub client that returns one fixed settings object, serialized from its host tree, dropped into the settings dialog's own `.settings-main` / `.settings-group-detail` / `.settings-detail-header` wrapper, with the app's own stylesheets in `src/styles/index.css` order, screenshotted in headless Edge. Nothing in the frame is drawn by hand. No Electron window was involved: this environment has no display and no Playwright install, so a running-app capture was not available to me.

Two real commits, checked out for the captures: **before = `80fa5e14`** (main, this branch's parent) and **after = `4b7b45a8`** (this PR's head). Both frames are 1280×1625 CSS px at 2×, **no crop** — the whole page including the `保存` row is in every frame — same language and same initial settings object.

zh-CN:

![before zh-CN: the page ends with a 各阶段思考强度 block of five selects, each on 跟随模型, then 保存](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/yuanzhou75/sciencediscovery/d0338760d31fd5b07c40c68a3572bf0379d764a2/shots/1279-head/before-zh.png)

![after zh-CN: the page ends with 阶段提示词覆盖 and 保存, no 各阶段思考强度 block](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/yuanzhou75/sciencediscovery/f5108a0528c37695b589655e21ca8e8d436249fc/shots/1279-head/after-zh.png)

en:

![before en: the page ends with a Thinking effort per stage block of five selects, each on Follow the model, then Save](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/yuanzhou75/sciencediscovery/683a870628029a0228a8f24a6cca57b894c49e13/shots/1279-head/before-en.png)

![after en: the page ends with Stage prompt overrides and Save, no Thinking effort per stage block](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/yuanzhou75/sciencediscovery/9ed70746699653ed43f3043439b889741d2226d1/shots/1279-head/after-en.png)

Both frames lack the 「单次调用 token」 row because main's `3529a555` removed it before this head; the pair differs only by this commit — the removed block and the page description that stops advertising it.

## Tests

- `tsc --noEmit` clean for `packages/schema`, `services/api`, `apps/desktop` and the root `tsconfig.tests.json`, on the rebased head.
- `apps/desktop` → `tests/idea-tree-settings.test.tsx`: 3 passed. The pane test now asserts `各阶段思考强度` and `跟随模型` are absent, that a save does not PUT `roleThinkingEfforts`, **and** that the single action row still carries `settings-actions is-end` (the assertion #1280 added; both survive the rebase conflicts).
- `services/evolve` → `tests/test_idea_research.py -k thinking_level`: 1 passed, on main's new `transport(system, payload)` shape. A research asks for no `reasoning_effort`, and a legacy settings payload carrying `roleThinkingEfforts` is not carried into the research.
- `py_compile` clean on the three touched Python files.
- `services/api/src/store/settings.test.ts` is tagged `os:linux`, so it skips on this Windows host (`platform-inapplicable`); the rewritten case there asserts the retired field is ignored on write and dropped on load, and CI runs it.

1282.author: yuanzhou75
1282.body:
Closes #1024

The import dialog's review card showed `source · objects · record bytes` and nothing else, although
`inspection.manifest.omissions` was already in the response and already typed on the client. This renders **every**
entry it carries, behind its count.

**What this PR delivers:** each manifest entry gets one row; the package's own text — sentences, ids, paths, digests,
reasons — is shown exactly as the package wrote it, while the count line, a row's family name, the hover hint, the
not-readable marker and the placeholder for an entry that cannot be described are the dialog's own words and follow
the interface language.

## Owner decision recorded here (2026-11-21)

Text that came **in the package** is shown as the package wrote it, and only text the dialog itself generates follows
the interface language. The omissions array is package content, so:

- **verbatim** — the sentences the exporter wrote (`科学记忆以摘要形式保留…`, `导出范围省略工作区文件：3。`,
  `validation evidence version 4 is unavailable`, `5 more entries could not be read…`), and the id, path, digest and
  reason of a reference row;
- **localized** — the count line (`未包含 N 项` / `Not included: N items`), the family name of a reference row
  (`工作区文件`, `产物`, `包内对象`, `演化检索`, `轨迹记录`, `文件版本`, `任务运行`, `审阅记录`), the hover
  explanation, the `（不是可读文本）` marker, and the `无法表示的值` / `unrepresentable value` placeholder.

This is deliberate. It is recorded in comment 7058847530 (2026-11-21T06:48:55Z) and in this section; it supersedes
comment 7056788266 (2026-11-21T03:43:01Z) and the review asks that went with it, because the owner decided package
text must not be re-authored by the client.

## What changes

This is **one commit** on top of `348b4db4` (the branch was squashed; the earlier history, including a commit message
with stray control characters that two reviews flagged, is gone).

- **the count is the manifest's own length.** `未包含 N 项` / `Not included: N items` prints
  `inspection.manifest.omissions.length`. Nothing is filtered out of the count, so a package whose entries are all
  reference-shaped cannot read as complete.
- **every entry gets a row.** A reference row (`<token>:<id>:<reason>`) becomes `<dialog family> · <package id/path> ·
  <package reason>`, e.g. `工作区文件 · results/trial-3.csv · ENOENT: no such file or directory, open '/data/trial-3.csv'`.
- **each shape is read with bounded fields, not by splitting every colon**, because the writers put free text there:
  `workspace:<session>:<path>:<reason…>`; `evolve:<run>:sha256:<digest>:<reason…>` (a candidate hash is
  `sha256:<64 hex>`), `evolve:<run>:<hash>:<reason…>` and `evolve:<message>`; `<token>:<id>:<reason…>`. An unknown
  shape falls back to the raw text. A colon inside a workspace path remains ambiguous — the upload sanitizer allows it
  — and that limitation is documented in the module; escaping it belongs in the writer, not in this dialog.
- **an entry that is not a string cannot break the dialog.** `parseManifest` only checks `Array.isArray`, so a crafted
  package can carry an object or a number. The row key is the index, and an entry that defeats both
  `JSON.stringify` (deep nesting) and `String()` (non-callable `toString`) renders the localized placeholder instead of
  throwing.
- **the rows start collapsed** behind the count, and a reference row explains itself on hover. An empty array still
  states `0` and draws no disclosure.
- **no scroll area of its own**; the dialog body already scrolls.

The parsing lives in `views/research-package-omissions.ts`. Untouched: the API, `packages/*`, the export path, and the
rest of the import card.

## Screenshots

**Component-level render, not a full application journey.** The real `ResearchPackage` import dialog mounted with a
stub client whose `/inspect` answer is one fixed inspection object, serialized from its host tree, loaded into headless
Edge with the app's own stylesheets (the `.modal-backdrop` / `.modal-panel` markup is the component's own). Nothing in
the frame is drawn by hand. No Electron window was involved: this environment has no display and no Playwright install,
so a running-app capture was not available to me.

**The two code commits these frames come from:** **before = `348b4db4`** (main, this PR's merge base) and
**after = `f1cf043d`** (this PR's head). The eight frames were re-rendered from both and are byte-identical to the
previous set, so they are current for this head rather than historical.

**Where the image files live:** all eight are pinned to **one** commit on the `shots/1024-import-omissions` branch —
`14ccbb2de268e8b7756bad30ea895068e3dc9c64` — which holds only these PNGs. That is a storage ref, not a code commit; it
replaces `f86d8334`, whose zh-CN expanded frame had been captured mid-fade (almost blank) and is re-captured there,
with the other seven byte-identical.

All frames: 1280×1000 CSS px at 2×, same viewport, same inspection object. The manifest carries **seven** entries:
three sentences the exporter wrote, and four reference rows (`workspace:` with an `ENOENT: …` reason, `artifact:` with
`Error: read failed`, `cas:`, and `evolve:` with a 64-hex `sha256:` digest).

**Before** (`5f21b213`) — the card ends at the meta line:

![before zh-CN: the import card shows only source · objects · record bytes](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/yuanzhou75/sciencediscovery/14ccbb2de268e8b7756bad30ea895068e3dc9c64/shots/1282-final2/before-zh.png)

**After, collapsed** (`f1cf043d`) — the count is the whole array; the rows are one click away:

![after zh-CN collapsed: 未包含 7 项 with a closed disclosure](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/yuanzhou75/sciencediscovery/14ccbb2de268e8b7756bad30ea895068e3dc9c64/shots/1282-final2/after-collapsed-zh.png)

![after en collapsed: Not included: 7 items with a closed disclosure](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/yuanzhou75/sciencediscovery/14ccbb2de268e8b7756bad30ea895068e3dc9c64/shots/1282-final2/after-collapsed-en.png)

**After, expanded** — the same render with the disclosure opened. The family names follow the dialog's language;
everything after them is the package's own text, including the Chinese sentences in the en frame — that is the
decision above, not a missed translation:

![after zh-CN expanded: seven rows — three package sentences, then 工作区文件/产物/包内对象/演化检索 rows with the package's ids and reasons](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/yuanzhou75/sciencediscovery/14ccbb2de268e8b7756bad30ea895068e3dc9c64/shots/1282-final2/after-expanded-zh.png)

![after en expanded: the same seven rows — English family names, package text verbatim (the Chinese sentences included)](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/yuanzhou75/sciencediscovery/14ccbb2de268e8b7756bad30ea895068e3dc9c64/shots/1282-final2/after-expanded-en.png)

**After, no omissions** — an empty array: the line states `0` and no disclosure is drawn:

![after zh-CN empty: 未包含 0 项 and no disclosure](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/yuanzhou75/sciencediscovery/14ccbb2de268e8b7756bad30ea895068e3dc9c64/shots/1282-final2/after-empty-zh.png)

![after en empty: Not included: 0 items and no disclosure](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/yuanzhou75/sciencediscovery/14ccbb2de268e8b7756bad30ea895068e3dc9c64/shots/1282-final2/after-empty-en.png)

**Not capturable:** the hover explanation is a native `title` tooltip, drawn by the OS and absent from a headless
capture. The tests pin each reference row's `title` instead.

## Tests

`apps/desktop` → `tests/research-package-trim.test.tsx`: **19 passed**, including:

- a five-entry manifest reports **5**, each entry has a row, the exporter's sentences appear verbatim, and no raw
  `workspace:`/`cas:`/`artifact:` token reaches the screen;
- a manifest made **only of reference rows** reports 3 and never `0`;
- a manifest carrying `{x:1}`, `123` and `{"toString": null}` renders three rows, shows each as text, and does not
  throw;
- an object with `toString: null` nested 5000 deep — which defeats `JSON.stringify` with `RangeError` and `String()`
  with `TypeError` — renders the localized placeholder instead of blanking the dialog;
- a `workspace:` row whose reason is `ENOENT: no such file or directory, open '/data/trial-3.csv'` keeps the path and
  the whole reason, and `artifact:<id>:Error: read failed` keeps its id;
- `evolve:<run>:sha256:<64-hex digest>:<reason>` keeps the run, the whole digest and the reason;
  `evolve:<run>:<hash>:<reason>` and `evolve:<message>` still work;
- an unknown family token named after an `Object.prototype` key (`constructor:abc:def`, `toString:x`) prints as
  written, with no family label invented for it.

Red-before-green, per the commits that introduced them: the count/filter case fails against `5b7754f`; the
`{"toString": null}` case fails against `e29bd64e` with `TypeError: Cannot convert object to primitive value`; the
deep-nesting case fails against the same head once the key fix is present. On this head, 19 pass, and both
`tsc -p apps/desktop/tsconfig.json --noEmit` and `tsc -p tsconfig.tests.json --noEmit` are clean.

The desktop cases are tagged `os:linux`, so a plain run on this Windows host skips them; the results above come from
the same runner with the host reported as linux/amd64.

1285.author: yuanzhou75
1285.body:
Closes #1281

Idea Tree's per-call ceiling (`maxTokensPerCall`, default 32768, range 256–32768) is gone: the settings page no longer shows it, the API neither returns nor accepts it, and the engine sends no `max_tokens`, so a call is bounded by whatever the model and its service default to.

## What removed what

- **Schema** — `IdeaTreeSettings`, `IdeaTreeSettingsDetails` and `UpdateIdeaTreeSettingsRequest` lose the field, as does `IdeaResearchSettings` (the settings echoed back with a research record).
- **Desktop** — the row and its two strings leave `IdeaTreeSettings.tsx`, `text/zh.ts` and `text/en.ts`. The write payload stops carrying the field.
- **Configuration** — `settings-catalog.ts` drops it from `idea_tree`'s field list; `agent-metadata.ts` drops the capability field and its "bounded token" wording; `system-adapters.ts` stops offering the number field; `discovery.ts` stops summarising it.
- **Normalizer** — `normalizeIdeaTreeSettings` no longer validates it, and `resolveIdeaTreeSettings` no longer fills a default for it.
- **Engine** — `transport()` loses its `ceiling` parameter and no longer writes `max_tokens` into the request body. `_ask` keeps a 32768 reservation for the total-budget check; that is a reservation, not a cap, and the comment says so.
- **Dead labels** — the shared `configuration-ui` message maps and `apps/web`'s i18n lose their `maxTokensPerCall` entries, which nothing could reach once the field left the catalog.

## Screenshots

**These are component-level renders, not a full application journey.** The real `IdeaTreeSettings` component was mounted through the repo's own Vite dev server against a stub `ApiClient` returning the settings payload the API served before this change, and captured in headless Edge. No hand-written markup, no design mock: what you see is the shipped component and the shipped stylesheets. The Electron window itself cannot be automated in this environment.

Both frames come from two real commits: **before `2a5b51a4`** (current main, the branch's base) and **after `ea063ede`** (this PR's first head, which carries every UI/source change). Same viewport (1240×2 CSS px wide at 2× device scale), same stub payload, same language per pair. The later commit `58c5b5fb` only fixes four call sites in `services/api/src/protocol-compatibility.test.ts` — no UI and no desktop source — so these captures still show this PR's UI.

Chinese — before: 研究范围 shows **单次调用 token 32768** under token 上限; after: the row is gone, token 上限 (the per-research budget) stays.

![before, zh: 单次调用 token row present](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/yuanzhou75/sciencediscovery/4b3870d5c5b1a3e752d03e14325bbbbd1d1ddd5f/shots/1281/before-zh.png)

![after, zh: the row is gone](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/yuanzhou75/sciencediscovery/4b3870d5c5b1a3e752d03e14325bbbbd1d1ddd5f/shots/1281/after-zh.png)

English — before: **Tokens per call 32768**; after: gone, Token limit stays.

![before, en: Tokens per call row present](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/yuanzhou75/sciencediscovery/4b3870d5c5b1a3e752d03e14325bbbbd1d1ddd5f/shots/1281/before-en.png)

![after, en: the row is gone](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/yuanzhou75/sciencediscovery/4b3870d5c5b1a3e752d03e14325bbbbd1d1ddd5f/shots/1281/after-en.png)

## Every remaining `maxTokensPerCall` in the tree, and why it stays

Left over on purpose:

| Where | Why |
| --- | --- |
| `packages/schema/src/evolution.ts:307`, `services/api/src/evolution/{proposal,sidecar,orchestrator,preflight}.ts` and their tests, `services/api/src/research-package-http.test.ts:364`, `test/api/evolve-thinking-journey.mjs:147` | Evolve's **own** `budget.maxTokensPerCall` — a different per-call ceiling for the evolution sidecar, unrelated to the Idea Tree setting. Out of scope by the issue's boundary. |
| `test/contract/baselines/legacy-linux.json:8640` | The recorded legacy-API snapshot. `test/contract/README.md` calls the baselines **read-only for agents** and says changing one needs human review; it records what the old API answered, so the field belongs there. Not touched. |
| `services/api/src/protocol-compatibility.test.ts:123` | A fixture that simulates a research record written by an older engine (`settings=dict(maxTokensPerCall=8,...)`). Kept deliberately: it is the case that shows an old record still parses. |
| `services/api/src/store/settings.ts:551`, `services/api/src/store/settings.test.ts:135–145` | The new legacy-tolerance test and the comment explaining it (below). |

Gone: the desktop page, both desktop dictionaries, the schema, the configuration catalog, capability metadata, the edit form, the discovery summary, the research record type, both message maps, the normalizer and the engine. `git grep maxTokensPerCall` now matches only the rows above.

## Upgrading from an older build

A stored settings row, or a stale client, may still carry the field. It is dropped silently rather than rejected, so an upgraded deployment reads its own catalog without a migration. `services/api/src/store/settings.test.ts` now pins exactly that: a stored object with `maxTokensPerCall: 8192` resolves to an object **without** the key and keeps the rest, and update payloads carrying 255 / 8192 / 32769 are ignored without throwing.

## Verification

- `pnpm --filter @sciencediscovery/schema build` clean; `services/api` `tsc --noEmit` clean; `apps/desktop` `tsc -p tsconfig.json --noEmit` clean; root `tsc -p tsconfig.tests.json --noEmit` clean.
- `services/api`: `src/configuration/*.test.ts` + `src/store/*.test.ts` — **441 / 441 pass**; the three suites the normalizer touches also pass as a group (29 / 29).
- `apps/desktop`: **1352 / 1352 pass**.
- **The engine change has its own evidence**: the suite cannot run here (no pytest, no network to install one), so the test that pins it was inverted rather than deleted — `test_idea_research.py` now asserts `'max_tokens' not in sent[0]`, and locally I ran the same call against the real `transport()` with `urlopen` stubbed and read the body: `body keys: ['messages']`. That printed assertion is what stands in for the suite until CI runs it.
- **The full `services/api` suite did not complete locally**: run as one glob it stalls inside `src/server.test.ts` (observed >18 min with no progress); run alone, `src/server.test.ts` completes. CI is the authority for the whole suite, and this PR does not claim otherwise.

## Notes

- **One consequence of the reservation, stated plainly:** because the reservation is a fixed 32768, a deployment that used to set a small per-call cap and a total budget somewhere between the prompt estimate and 32768 will now hit the budget refusal where the old, smaller reservation let it through. The request itself is unchanged by this (it carries no cap); the difference is only how much the total-budget check sets aside before the call.
- Two optional review notes are left for a later cleanup rather than fixed here, because pushing to a PR already in the merge queue would eject it and discard both approvals: `test_idea_research.py:303` hard-codes `32768` where importing `OUTPUT_RESERVATION_TOKENS` would keep the test from drifting, and `research.py` carries one stray blank line before `class IdeaTreeEngine`.
- `maxTokens` (the per-research budget) is untouched, and so is every Evolve budget field.
- `maxTokensPerCall` is removed from the public `GET/PUT /api/settings/idea-tree` payload. A client that still sends it is ignored rather than rejected — the same tolerance the stored-settings path has.

1285.title: feat(idea-tree): drop the per-call token cap

1286.author: yuanzhou75
1286.body:
Closes #1250

The desktop client had no trace of session archive: the list was fetched with `state=active`, the row menu offers only 重命名 / 导出 / 删除, and an archived Session is read-only on the server. So a Session archived in the web client **disappeared** from the desktop app — no way to find it, no action to bring it back. This is the missing half of a feature the server and the web client already have.

## The shape, after the owner's review

Three things the first cut did are now deliberately gone, because they made the feature harder to use rather than easier:

- **No 活跃 / 已归档 / 全部 filter.** The sidebar is the active set, full stop. A three-way switch duplicated a page that should own the archived ones, and a remembered `已归档` opened the app on an empty list.
- **No confirmation before archiving.** Archiving is reversible in two clicks; the dialog only slowed it down. Deleting still asks — that one cannot be undone.
- **Archived Sessions are not in the sidebar at all.** They are in 设置 › 会话管理, the way 导出记录 is: a page for a set that is no longer part of the everyday list.

## What changed (desktop only)

- **`api/sessions.ts`** — `archiveSession` / `restoreSession`, posting to the existing `/archive` and `/restore` routes and returning the Session the service stored.
- **`app/session-filter.ts`** (new) — the membership helpers the listing needs: what a filtered read proves about the whole set, which Sessions belong to a Project, and what to forget when a Project goes. Nothing here remembers a user preference any more.
- **`app/use-workspace.ts`** — the listing is read unfiltered, because the artifact catalog may only be pruned against whole membership; the sidebar draws the active subset of it. Archiving: `archiveSession` archives straight away and reports the server's 409 verbatim when a run is still going; `restoreSession` returns its promise and `deleteSession` takes an `onSettled`, which `mutate` runs after the list refresh it already awaits — that is what lets the settings page redraw from the server instead of guessing.
- **`views/Sidebar.tsx`** — a row offers 归档 (active) or 恢复 (archived), drawn with its own inline box icon beside 重命名 / 导出 / 删除, because the design system has no icon font and the 导出 entry is inline SVG too. While that Session is running the entry is `disabled` with its reason, rather than letting the server answer 409.
- **`views/settings/system/Sessions.tsx`** (new) + **`views/SystemSettingsDialog.tsx`** — 设置 › 会话管理, in 工作区 above 导出记录: the archived Sessions of the Projects in scope, newest archive first, with the same scope control and search field 导出记录 uses. A row opens the Session read-only, 恢复 sends it back to 活跃 where the conversation carries on, and 彻底删除 goes through the workspace's own confirmation — the same one the ⋯ menu uses, so the two cannot drift apart.
- **`App.tsx` / `views/Composer.tsx`** — an archived Session opens read-only: a banner above the composer (`archivedBanner`), and the composer gated by `readOnlyReason` so the placeholder says why instead of failing a send. The export entry stays available — it only reads.
- **`views/RowMenu.tsx`** — menu entries can be `disabled` (with `aria-disabled`), which the run-active case needs.
- **`text/zh.ts`, `text/en.ts`** — both locales, including the new 会话管理 page and its empty state.
- **`styles/design.css`, `styles/session-management.css`** (new) — the icon row and the settings list.

## Where the consequences come from

Not invented here — the copy repeats what the service already does:

- `services/api/src/store.ts:6385` — an archived Session is read-only; writes throw `Session is archived and read-only`.
- `services/api/src/http/index.ts:3315-3317` — archiving tears down the Session's scientific-environment kernels with `Session was archived; persistent memory was lost`.
- `services/api/src/http/index.ts:3311-3312` — archiving is refused with `409 Cannot change archive state during an active run`, which is why the action is disabled while running.

## Not in this PR — a separate issue

`store.ts:6400-6410`: `archiveSession` stops the Session's notifications and the comment states *"Restore does not reopen it."* `restoreSession` then only clears `archivedAt`. Whether a restored Session should wake for notifications again is a product decision, not a client fix — reported separately, untouched here.

## Verification

Run in WSL (Ubuntu, linux-amd64, Node v22.23.4) against this head's tree:

- `tsc -p apps/desktop --noEmit` — clean.
- `tsc -p tsconfig.tests.json --noEmit` — clean (it does not cover `apps/desktop`, so it is a regression check, not evidence for these files).
- `node test/check-e2e-meta.mjs` — 97 spec file(s), 0 error(s).
- `apps/desktop` suites `session-management` (new) + `session-archive` + `sidebar`: **24 tests / 24 pass**. The new four pin the row the page draws: the title, the Project and the three actions; an unnamed Session shown in the interface language rather than as a blank row; exactly one action drawn as destructive; and the directory entry itself, since a group missing from `settings.system.groups` would be a page nobody can open.

## Review round — six findings, and the one red gate

The review found six things and UT found one. All seven are fixed; each thread has its own reply and is resolved.

- **`b11011b2` — the settings tree's own case** now lists 会话管理 between 超时 and 导出记录. This was the single UT failure after the transition out of draft (job `137528122489`: 8144 planned, 8143 passed).
- **`f7220e81` — the inbox.** 会话管理 scoped itself over `state.projects`, which the server keeps the inbox out of, so a Session archived from 会话 — where every first conversation lands — had no row on the page that is supposed to hold it. The page takes `state.inboxProject` as its own prop now.
- **`13f68cfc` — the welcome page.** `readOnlyReason` moved into `composerProps`, which the landing page spreads too, and `sendMessage` refuses an archived Session at the send: an archived Session with no transcript used to draw a writable composer.
- **`ac7388ca` — membership.** The listing is read unfiltered and the sidebar is drawn from the active subset, so the artifact catalog is pruned against every Session that still exists. Before, the set could only grow and a Session deleted from another client left a 产物 group pointing at nothing.
- **`a1245c95` — the filter's leftovers.** Storage key, guard, read, write, stylesheet rules, four labels, and the archive confirmation's copy are gone; the case that could not fail is deleted instead of dressed up.
- **`486b2a27` — the re-read.** The first attempt at this fix (`f7220e81`) still kept `projects` in the effect's dependencies, so the identity changed on every refresh and the effect re-ran anyway. The arrays live in a ref now and the read depends on a key that changes only when the set of Projects does.

Verified on this head with the full desktop suite, not a slice: `tsc -p apps/desktop --noEmit` clean, `tsc -p tsconfig.tests.json --noEmit` clean, **1466 tests / 1466 pass** (the hint's own mount test included).

## Screenshots

**UI hold:** approving this PR needs the **code owner to look at these captures**. It is a UI change; a code-only approval is not enough.

Frames 1–3 were rendered from `3772dc12`, the head they record. `RowMenu.tsx`, `Sidebar.tsx`, `views/settings/system/Sessions.tsx` and the two stylesheets are byte-identical between that head and the current one, so what they show still holds at `70ca40f2`: the real desktop bundle (`vite build` in `apps/desktop`), served from the local API's own origin so `/api` is same-origin, driven by Playwright's Chromium at viewport 1440×940 with `deviceScaleFactor: 2`, one browser context per locale with `sciencediscovery-desktop:locale` set before the first paint. The stack is the API from this tree on `http://127.0.0.1:4310` — **legacy backend (`--no-jiuwenswarm`), repository-default data directory (`.sciencediscovery-data`, not isolated)**. The workspace is real data from earlier local runs. One Session was archived through `POST /api/sessions/:id/archive` so the settings page has a row; it was created in the inbox on purpose, because that is the Project the page did not reach before `f7220e81`, and it is what frame 3 shows — the inbox in the scope select, and its archived Session in the list with 恢复 one press away.
